articles.title: Eka is worth $1.45B thanks to a physical AI model that has experts raving | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Robots still aren’t that good at picking things up, despite billions of dollars of investment and endless videos fed into deep learning models.
That may be about to change, thanks to a manipulation architecture built by Eka Robotics, which encompasses a force-sensitive gripper and a new kind of deep-learning model. Founded by MIT professor Pulkit Agrawal and former Google DeepMind researcher Tuomas Haarnoja, the startup just closed an $150 million Series A round that values it at $1.45 billion post-money, led by venture funds a16z and F-Prime.
“They are already exceeding superhuman performance for certain tasks, and so we think over the next few months there will be superhuman performance in many dexterous manipulation tasks,” Raghu Raghuram, the a16z general partner who co-led the fundraising round, told TechCrunch.
In an era of never-ending robotic demonstrations, Eka’s capabilities are shocking veteran robot builders.
Kris Hauser, a professor at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, said it had a “wow factor” compared to other robot demos he saw recently. The Eka robot “was able to adapt to a large number of different objects without retraining,” Hauser said, adding that it also had an aspect of “humanness, creepy humanness that it would try over and over again if it failed the first time.”

articles.title: Anvisa aprova novo remédio contra câncer de pulmão; Brasil é o 2º país a liberar terapia
articles.summary:
A Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária (Anvisa) aprovou, na segunda-feira (19), o telisotuzumabe vedotina, comercializado como Emrelis, medicamento destinado a adultos com câncer de pulmão de não pequenas células (CPNPC) avançado ou metastático. Com a decisão, o Brasil se tornou o segundo país a autorizar a terapia, depois dos Estados Unidos, onde o produto recebeu aprovação acelerada em maio de 2025.
Desenvolvido pela farmacêutica americana AbbVie, o medicamento é indicado para pacientes com tumores do tipo não escamoso que apresentam alta expressão da proteína c-Met e que já passaram por tratamento sistêmico anterior. A identificação desse biomarcador é fundamental para determinar quais pacientes podem se beneficiar da terapia.
A aprovação brasileira foi baseada no estudo clínico de fase 2 LUMINOSITY. Na pesquisa, a taxa de resposta objetiva chegou a 34,6% entre os pacientes com alta expressão de c-Met. Isso significa que essa proporção apresentou redução mensurável do tumor, e não que os participantes tenham sido curados.
Segundo a AbbVie, a previsão é que o medicamento chegue ao mercado brasileiro no primeiro semestre de 2027, após as etapas regulatórias necessárias para a comercialização.

articles.title: 970,000 Medi-Cal Members Affected by Paradigm Healthcare Data Breach
articles.summary:
Paradigm Healthcare Services has told the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) that a data breach discovered last year affected more than 970,000 people.
San Francisco-based Paradigm processes billing for Medi-Cal, California’s Medicaid program, under a data use agreement with the California Department of Health Care Services (DHCS). It also maintains Medi-Cal member identification numbers on the department’s behalf.
The company says it became aware of unauthorized access to its local network on October 13, 2025. “On August 18, 2026, we determined that certain files containing select individuals’ protected health information may have been accessed by an unauthorized party between October 8, 2025, and October 15, 2025,” Paradigm said.
The compromised files contained names, dates of birth, gender, and Medi-Cal member identification numbers. Paradigm says its online service documentation and billing platform, Student Health Network (SHN), was not impacted.
Paradigm’s notification letters are dated September 14, 2026, roughly 11 months after the intrusion was detected. “We have no evidence that any of your information has been used to commit fraud or identity theft as a result of this incident,” the company said.
The notice doesn’t name the threat actor, explain how the attackers gained access, or say whether data was exfiltrated. Paradigm says it took certain systems offline, notified law enforcement, and brought in outside incident response experts.

articles.title: Scientists recreate a bizarre quantum effect that stops a particle cold
articles.summary:
Scientists recreate a bizarre quantum effect that stops a particle cold
- Date:
- October 13, 2026
- Source:
- University of Oxford
- Summary:
- Oxford physicists have recreated a bizarre quantum effect in which a particle responds to a magnetic field without ever traveling through it. Using a hybrid quantum computer, they demonstrated how introducing a simulated magnetic flux could completely halt a particle's movement through quantum interference. The experiment brings a decades-old prediction into a new setting where matter and quantum fields influence one another.
- Share:
A particle does not have to pass through a magnetic field to be influenced by it. That surprising feature of quantum physics has now been recreated by researchers at the University of Oxford, who used a hybrid quantum computer to demonstrate how an invisible magnetic influence can bring a simulated particle's movement to a complete stop.
The experiment reproduced a phenomenon known as the Aharonov-Bohm effect, in which a charged particle traveling around a region containing magnetic flux experiences a measurable change in its quantum state, even though its path never takes it through the magnetic field itself.
The Oxford team achieved this using a quantum system that combines qubits, the basic units of quantum information, with quantum oscillators, which represent vibrating motion. articles.title: A cleaner path to rare earth metals
articles.summary:
A cleaner path to rare earth metals
Tomás Villalón Jr. ’14
Tomás Villalón Jr. ’14 was raised in San Antonio, Texas, but vividly remembers smog hanging over the city his family came from—Monterrey, Mexico, a steel manufacturing and metal fabrication hub. Even as a child, he realized it was problematic to breathe that air.
“I’m motivated because I’ve seen what metal-making does,” says Villalón, who majored in materials science and engineering. He started thinking about sustainable metallurgy senior year while working at Boston Metal, an MIT spinoff focused on decarbonizing steelmaking. In 2019 he cofounded Phoenix Tailings, which has developed an efficient process for extracting rare earth metals from mining waste.
“The mining ecosystem by itself makes over several billion tons of waste,” says Villalón, who serves as chief technology officer. (Others on the founding team are Michelle Chao ’17, Nick Myers, and Anthony Balladon.) “We have to get rid of this pollution.”
The company asserts that its proprietary electrochemical technique for processing rare earths generates no toxins and is carbon-free when fueled by renewables.

Oura adds two new cardiovascular health tracking features to its smart rings

Yet when asked about "awareness" instead, people judged humans and AI much more similarly.
- Share:
Even when artificial intelligence behaves exactly like a human, people are reluctant to consider it conscious, according to a new study from Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (LMU).
As artificial intelligence becomes more advanced, reports of AI systems misleading users, working together, or appearing to pursue independent goals are becoming increasingly common. These behaviors often lead people to describe AI as though it can think, feel, or make decisions for itself. But does behaving like a human actually convince people that a machine has consciousness?
New research from LMU suggests that people make a clear distinction between displaying intelligent behavior and possessing a conscious mind, even when humans and AI act in precisely the same way.

articles.title: Build a semantic layer for agentic AI on AWS with AtScale and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Build a semantic layer for agentic AI on AWS with AtScale and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
In the first post in this series, we built a semantic layer on AWS using Stardog’s knowledge graph over Amazon Aurora and Amazon Redshift. We ran a Strands agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore against that layer. The second post kept the same customer 360 (C360) pattern and swapped in Denodo’s data virtualization platform, extending the source mix to include an on-premises PostgreSQL cluster. This post uses the same C360 pattern again, with AtScale as the semantic layer.
AtScale takes a different shape from the first two. The semantic model is dimensional (dimensions, hierarchies, and measures) rather than a graph of triples or a set of views. AtScale authors the model in the Semantic Modeling Language, an open, YAML-based specification versioned in Git, and exposes it simultaneously, from a single deployed model, over three protocols: SQL, XML for Analysis (XMLA), and the Model Context Protocol (MCP). The Strands agent and the business intelligence (BI) tools the enterprise already uses get the same computed answer from the same definitions.
The rest of the pattern carries over from the earlier posts. A foundation model on Amazon Bedrock (Anthropic Claude Sonnet 4.6 for the walkthrough) plans and writes queries. articles.title: A champion for brain injury patients
articles.summary:
A champion for brain injury patients
Alissa Totman ’13
Alissa Totman ’13 was a sophomore when she joined MIT BrainTrust, a student-run organization that connects Institute undergraduates and people with brain injuries for support and socializing. “That group was a great way to learn about the human experience of what people go through when they experience a brain injury,” she says. And it laid the foundation for her life’s work.
Today, Totman is a physician specializing in brain injury medicine at the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center, where she treats adults with head trauma, stroke, brain tumors, and more.
She is also the founder of Synapse, a nonprofit focused on providing support for such individuals. The organization grew out of a group she started with Jaclyn Konopka ’14 during medical school at Stanford, and Totman launched it as a national service organization in 2016, while pursuing her master’s degree in public health at Harvard.
There are now chapters at 28 universities across the country—and Totman still runs the organization. “There’s a big need for more resources like this,” she says.

articles.title: US orders federal agencies to remove China’s DeepSeek AI from their systems | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
The U.S. has ordered federal civilian agencies to stop purchasing services and products developed by Chinese AI startup DeepSeek and remove them from government IT systems over national security concerns tied to the Chinese AI startup’s operations in China, according to the Department of Homeland Security. The order goes beyond banning DeepSeek’s own product, and covers third-party products and services built using DeepSeek technology, though agencies can request exceptions.
The DHS raised concerns about DeepSeek’s handling of user data, warning that sensitive information from U.S. government users could potentially be accessible to Chinese authorities under Chinese law, the order said.
The move comes amid intensifying tech competition in AI between the U.S. and China. The Chinese AI model challenges its U.S. rivals, including OpenAI and Meta, with low-cost open-weight models.
China pushed back against the U.S.’s move. Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said Tuesday that Beijing opposes “overstretching the concept of national security and politicizing technology and trade issues,” according to an official briefing. “We will resolutely safeguard the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese enterprises,” the spokesperson added.

Artificial Intelligence
Securing AI agent identity with X.509 PKI on AWS
When AI agents access databases, APIs, and sensitive business operations, establishing cryptographic identity through X.509 public key infrastructure (PKI) becomes a critical requirement. The core challenge is proving which agent made a request, preventing forgery between agents, and confirming that each agent acts only on behalf of an authorized user. Traditional approaches such as sharing API keys between components or passing OAuth tokens through agent chains fall short of the zero-trust requirements that enterprise deployments demand.
Multi-agent AI frameworks increasingly use the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to connect agents to external tools and data sources. MCP defines how a large language model (LLM)-powered agent invokes tools such as database queries or email operations. However, MCP has no built-in authentication standard. It is transport-agnostic by design. This creates a critical gap: Without proper identity mechanisms, any component could impersonate an agent, replay intercepted credentials, or invoke tools without authorization.
In this post, we show you how to address this gap using Keyfactor EJBCA combined with AWS services. EJBCA is a PKI platform that supports high-availability deployment, REST API automation, and Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP) validation. articles.title: Nebraska native explores galaxies far, far away
articles.summary:
Nebraska native explores galaxies far, far away
Megan Donahue ’85
Growing up on a small farm in Nebraska, Megan Donahue ’85 discovered the wider world by reading her way through her local library. Today, she is learning how the wider universe works by studying galaxy clusters.
Donahue discovered her passion for physics in that library at age 12 and started her path into astronomy thanks to “a providential interaction.” Through MIT’s Undergraduate Research Opportunities Program, she got introduced to cutting-edge x-ray imaging—work she found “really cool.”
Now a professor of physics and astronomy at Michigan State University, she researches galaxy clusters and baryonic matter (matter made of protons and neutrons, as opposed to dark matter) in an effort to learn more about the composition of the universe and its evolution.
“Clusters of galaxies are very large scoops of the universe,” says Donahue, who served as president of the American Astronomical Society from 2018 to 2020. “It’s like taking a sample from the ocean. If you’re trying to find out the average composition of the ocean’s water, you’d want to study as big a scoop as possible.”

articles.title: Introducing tsrs: a Port of TypeScript to Rust
articles.summary:
Introducing tsrs: A port of TypeScript to Rust
Cloudflare and VoidZero are now working with Max Schwenk of Owner.com on tsrs, a Rust port of the TypeScript compiler. We are doing this work in close collaboration with the TypeScript team, and incubating tsrs as part of the Oxc JavaScript compiler toolchain.
Our goal is to help developers spend less time waiting for their code to be checked and more time building. Making TypeScript faster and more memory-efficient also helps bring complete development environments to more places, including right in your browser.
To be clear, we are not forking TypeScript. We believe the TypeScript team should remain in full control of the language’s design and direction. They have maintained a long-term vision while guiding TypeScript’s adoption across the JavaScript community. We do not want to change that.
The TypeScript team can move quite fast on many things, but for some features they may spend years intentionally exploring options and making prototypes before picking the right implementation. A Rust port has to follow those decisions closely, or it will eventually fall apart and become incompatible. We have to preserve the TypeScript language strictly based on its original implementation – and the TypeScript team should remain solely responsible for deciding what that looks like.

Most AI incident tools still leave a key decision to humans
An AI SRE agent can help troubleshoot an incident. But can you trust it to decide on its own when something needs attention?
Most teams treat agent autonomy as a yes or no question. For incident response, it is a progression with three phases, and many agents in production sit earlier on it than the teams running them realize. Most AI SRE tools still stop short of the final phase.
On Thursday, October 22, The New Stack hosts a live webinar with Raaz Dwivedi, co-founder and CTO of Traversal and an assistant professor at Cornell Tech. His team applies causal AI and agentic reasoning to production incidents. He will walk through where the industry sits on that progression and what it takes to move up.
You have successfully registered for the webinar.
The three phases of agent autonomy
Invoked: copilots, chat interfaces, and CLIs that wait for an on-call engineer to open them and ask a question mid-incident.
Background: scheduled jobs, alert rules, and triggers that fire on conditions someone predicted in advance.
Proactive: agents that decide for themselves when an incident needs attention, without waiting to be invoked or scheduled.
The first two phases share a limit. Each depends on a person noticing that something is wrong, or on someone predicting the right condition ahead of time. Proactive agents remove that dependency.

Artificial Intelligence
Discover tools at runtime with AWS Agent Registry
Runtime discovery with AWS Agent Registry can help address a problem that agent demos might hide. Hardcoded tools work fine for a handful, start to degrade at a few dozen, and become unmanageable beyond that. Enterprise systems expose hundreds of internal APIs for pricing, support, orders, inventory, and customer data. In these systems, the model can spend more tokens disambiguating tool names than reasoning about the user’s request. Each new capability requires a code change in the orchestrator, a redeploy, and a coordinated release across teams that would much rather ship on their own cadence.
This pattern can arise across enterprise software as a service (SaaS) engagements where teams expose large internal API surfaces to agentic consumers. Build-time wiring can become a bottleneck as the catalog expands. One approach is to change how the orchestrator accesses its tools: instead of compiling every tool into the agent, the agent can discover relevant tools at runtime.
AWS Agent Registry is a managed service for cataloging and discovering Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, agents, and agent skills. Publishers register protocol-specific descriptors and searchable descriptions. At runtime, an orchestrator can search approved, discoverable records and use the returned endpoint and descriptor content to construct a client. articles.title: Ex-OpenAI Worker Accused of Bugging Conference Room Planned to Fly to Saudi Arabia, Prosecutors Say
articles.summary:
A former OpenAI engineer charged with secretly installing a recording device in a conference room to glean company details had been “mere days” away from absconding to Saudi Arabia before his arrest last week, federal prosecutors revealed in new court filings.
Abdulrahman Alfozan’s wife and young son also left the country the day after the 35-year-old Saudi national’s arrest, traveling on a one-way ticket booked and paid for by a Saudi military official, prosecutors said in a memo Sunday seeking his continued detention.
“Ultimately, the defendant has little incentive to remain in the United States to see this case through,” federal prosecutors wrote. “He has ample resources —including his significant compensation from a decade of high-tech employment in the Bay Area and at least two bank accounts in Saudi Arabia — and what appears to be considerable support from a foreign government.”
A federal judge in San Francisco sided with prosecutors Monday, denying a request by Alfozan’s lawyers to release him to home confinement. His next court date is Nov.
Alfozan’s lawyer William Pernik argued in court that his client had strong ties to the U.S. and was “weeks away from achieving every immigrant’s dream” — U.S. citizenship.
Alfozan had a naturalization interview with federal officials scheduled next month and has been a lawful permanent resident since 2020, his lawyers said in their legal filings. He has also lived in the U.S. for 15 years and attended MIT and the University of Cali…

articles.title: Access OpenAI GPT models on Amazon Bedrock from Canada with cross-Region inference | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Access OpenAI GPT models on Amazon Bedrock from Canada with cross-Region inference
Canadian organizations building generative AI applications on Amazon Bedrock often need the latest foundation models (FMs), such as OpenAI GPT-6.1, OpenAI GPT-6, and GPT-5.6, accessible from the Canadian AWS Regions. With Amazon Bedrock cross-Region inference (CRIS), you can now access these models from Canada. OpenAI GPT-5.6 models (Sol, Terra, and Luna), GPT-6 (Astra, Sol, and Luna), and GPT-6.1 Sol are available from the Canada (Central) and Canada West (Calgary) Regions. Inference is processed in North America, with data-residency controls described later in this post.
Cross-Region inference is a capacity mechanism. Your application calls the Amazon Bedrock Runtime endpoint in your source Region. Amazon Bedrock then routes the request to a supported destination Region for processing. With this approach, you get access to a broader capacity pool that can help your application sustain throughput during demand spikes. You don’t need to manage destination Region routing in your application.
In this post, we walk through the GPT-5.6, GPT-6, and GPT-6.1 models available from Canada and the cross-Region inference profiles that serve them. We then show how to set up permissions and invoke the models with the OpenAI Responses API, Chat Completions API, and the Amazon Bedrock Converse API. For the Responses API, we include streaming and tool-use examples. Finally, we cover how…

articles.title: Japan launches mission to bring home a piece of the Martian moon Phobos
articles.summary:
Japan launched a $578 million mission Monday on a five-year expedition to land on the largest moon of Mars and retrieve samples for return to Earth, a daring international project that could yield new insights into the formation of the Solar System.
The robotic Martian Moons eXploration mission, known as MMX, lifted off at 3:41 pm EDT Monday (4:41 am Japan Standard Time Tuesday) from Tanegashima Space Center in southern Japan.
The MMX spacecraft rode into orbit atop a 207-foot-tall (63-meter) H3 rocket, Japan’s flagship launch vehicle. The rocket assigned to MMX debuted a new souped-up configuration with four strap-on solid rocket boosters, full-throttle main engines, and an extended payload shroud to accommodate the demands of Japan’s heaviest and most ambitious interplanetary mission to date.
The rocket’s upper stage accelerated the MMX spacecraft to a top speed of more than 24,000 mph, fast enough to break free of Earth’s gravitational pull for the 10-month voyage to Mars. The nearly 9,900-pound (4.5-metric ton) spacecraft—two-thirds of its mass comprised of propellant—separated from the H3 rocket about 71 minutes after liftoff.
Hiroshi Yamakawa, president of the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), declared the launch a success. “A long journey of five years has just started,” Yamakawa said.
MMX established contact with ground controllers, unfurled its solar panels, and was in a “very stable condition” soon after separating from the H3 rocket, according to Yasuhiro …

articles.title: Cómo se verían Las Guerreras K-pop en el universo de Dragon Ball Super: Beerus
articles.summary:
El estreno de Dragon Ball Super: Beerus abre una posibilidad para que los seguidores del anime imaginen a Las Guerreras K-pop dentro del universo de Goku y Vegeta.
Con referencias visuales y un pedido preciso, una herramienta de inteligencia artificial (IA) puede crear una escena de combate que enfrente al grupo con Beerus en un escenario espacial.
El procedimiento puede realizarse desde un navegador actualizado, sin instalar archivos de origen desconocido ni programas externos que soliciten permisos innecesarios.
Cuál es el primer paso para recrear imágenes de Las Guerreras K-pop
El primer paso es reunir una imagen grupal de Las Guerreras K-pop donde se distingan los rostros, los peinados, las prendas y los accesorios de cada integrante.
Una toma de cuerpo entero o desde la cintura permite que el generador identifique mejor las diferencias entre las protagonistas y reduzca la posibilidad de repetir caras o mezclar los vestuarios.
Además, se debe tener una referencia de Beerus, Goku y Vegeta. La imagen debe mostrar elementos reconocibles de cada personaje, como las orejas y el atuendo del Dios de la Destrucción, el uniforme naranja de Goku y la armadura de Vegeta.
Si la escena incluirá transformaciones, conviene que las referencias ya exhiban el cabello azul y las auras de energía correspondientes.

articles.title: AI’s Midas problem: When code is free, features are worthless
articles.summary:
AI’s Midas problem: When code is free, features are worthless
Every team that adopted Claude Code, Cursor, or Copilot to produce more code has the same problem: When output is free, offering volume stops being a viable strategy. In fact, teams accelerating their software development with AI may be giving up the very thing that makes their software valuable.
It’s time to remember what makes software valuable and why racing to produce a mountain of code and features leads to failure.
The Midas touch
In Ovid’s tale, Midas, king of Phrygia, took in the missing satyr Silenus, whom Phrygian peasants had found drunk, granted him ten days of hospitality, and then returned him to Dionysus. In return, he was offered the reward of his choice: whatever he wished for. Famously, he wished that everything he touched would turn to gold.
Testing his new ability on an oak twig and then a stone, Midas was delighted. Nathaniel Hawthorne, who retold the myth for children in 1851, added a rose garden: His Midas turns every bloom to gold, still delighted, though his daughter Marygold mourns that the roses no longer smell sweet. In both versions, the celebration ends at the table, where food and drink turn to gold in his hands. That’s when Midas realized his reward was a bane, not a blessing, and asked to be rid of it.
Many leaders who force-fed AI to developers are now coming to a realization similar to that of Midas.
Though the process is gradual, many organizations and leaders who force-fed AI to…

articles.title: High spectrum costs squeeze African telecom investment and digital growth
articles.summary: Africa’s mobile networks have expanded significantly over the past decade, bringing coverage to more people. But wider coverage has not translated into widespread internet use or network quality on par with other regions. A new report by the GSMA, Spectrum Policy in Africa: Enabling Investment and Empowering Consumers Through Effective Spectrum Pricing , identifies the high cost of accessing radio spectrum—the invisible radio frequencies that carry mobile calls and internet data—as a central bottleneck. African mobile operators pay significantly more for relatively less spectrum, leaving them with limited capacity to expand or improve service quality. According to GSMA Intelligence, spectrum costs consume 0.82% of mobile operators’ revenue per 100 MHz in Africa, compared with 0.66% in the rest of the world. Meanwhile, African operators hold an average of about 570 MHz of spectrum below 7 GHz, 24% less than the global peer average of approximately 750 MHz. The imbalance extends beyond price and availability to licence duration. Only nine African countries routinely grant spectrum licences lasting 20 years or more, while licences of 20 years or indefinite duration are standard across Europe, North America and developed Asian markets. Lowering spectrum fees could free up vital capital for network expansion , but lower fees alone do not guarantee better connectivity. articles.title: Entre expandir sus modelos de IA por todo el mundo o protegerlos, China tiene muy clara su decisión
articles.summary:
El Gobierno chino se está preparando para dar un volantazo. Durante los últimos dos años su estrategia para competir con EEUU en el ámbito de la inteligencia artificial (IA) se ha sostenido sobre la distribución a gran escala de modelos con pesos abiertos que pueden ser ejecutados localmente. Su apuesta pasa por tener los modelos más baratos, personalizables y accesibles con el propósito de ser los más desplegados, y, así, debilitar a sus competidores estadounidenses desde un punto de vista económico.
Por el momento no hay ningún indicio que nos invite a prever que la estrategia de China va a cambiar en lo que se refiere a su apuesta por los modelos de IA con pesos abiertos, pero el Gobierno liderado por Xi Jinping planea introducir un cambio muy importante en su itinerario. Y es que, según SCMP, ha presentado un borrador que contempla prohibiciones y restricciones a la exportación de 23 tecnologías vinculadas estrechamente al desarrollo de la IA.
Esta iniciativa está siendo dirigida por los ministerios de Comercio y Ciencia y Tecnología, e involucra a los modelos de IA, los agentes y las tecnologías de diseño de semiconductores. Lo que persigue China es proteger sus tecnologías más avanzadas en un contexto en el que la IA y los chips son cada vez más importantes desde un punto de vista estratégico. Si esta iniciativa sale adelante, y es muy probable que lo haga en ausencia de una oposición real a la postura del Gobierno, podemos esperar que algunas de sus tecnologías más ava…

articles.title: Fausses cagnottes : attention aux arnaques qui profitent des pillages du 17 octobre
articles.summary:
Les pillages survenus ce week-end à travers la France ont laissé un certain nombre de commerçants complètement dévastés. Marchandises volées, investissements partis en fumée, vitrines cassées, agressions physiques : les conséquences sont lourdes pour les commerçants touchés, qui doivent désormais faire face aux dégâts, aussi bien matériels que psychologiques. Face à cette situation, les cagnottes de soutien se sont multipliées. Certaines ont été mises en place par les commerçants eux-mêmes, tandis que d’autres sont mises en ligne à l’initiative de personnes désirant aider. Malheureusement, certains lancent aussi de fausses cagnottes, autrement dit, des arnaques.
Des escrocs profitent de la détresse des commerçants
Un gérant d’un magasin Micromania situé à Nice a été victime de pilleurs. Il a été agressé physiquement, tandis que son magasin a été pillé et ses vitrines cassées. Face aux images de l’agression et du pillage, mais aussi du courage dont l’homme a fait preuve, plusieurs personnes ont lancé des cagnottes afin de lui venir en aide. Cependant, le gérant a alerté sur la prolifération de fausses cagnottes en ligne.
Il explique dans une story Instagram : « Mon équipe et moi, on est très touchés par le soutien, merci pour ce que vous faites. Maintenant, je vois des cagnottes en ligne, je ne suis au courant de rien, personne ne m’a contacté, elles ne sont pas de mon fait. Prenez soin de vous. Évitez ce genre d’arnaque, ne vous faites pas avoir. Pour le moment, rien n’est fa…

articles.title: Marshall Heston 120 : la finition Cream s'invite sur la barre de son haut de gamme
articles.summary:
Marshall Heston 120 : la finition Cream s'invite sur la barre de son haut de gamme
Plus claire et résolument désirable, la finition Cream arrive le 20 octobre sur la Heston 120, la barre de son Dolby Atmos la plus ambitieuse de Marshall. De quoi transformer le modèle en véritable objet de design pour le salon, et l'occasion de revenir sur un produit qui revendique son esthétique autant que ses performances home cinéma.
Marshall a toujours puisé dans l'esthétique de ses amplis pour dessiner ses enceintes. La Heston 120 ne fait pas exception. Chez Marshall, une barre de son n'est jamais un simple accessoire de téléviseur : c'est un objet que l'on expose, au même titre qu'une guitare accrochée au mur ou qu'un ampli posé dans un coin du salon. Jusqu'ici réservée à une livrée noire, la barre de son s'offre une déclinaison Cream. Plus lumineuse, cette nouvelle finition ouvre la Heston 120 à des univers déco plus clairs et contemporains. Le reste de l'appareil, lui, ne change pas d'un hertz.
Une couleur qui modifie le statut de l'objet
La finition Cream fait plus que rafraîchir une fiche produit. Associée aux commandes physiques crantées et aux cadrans inspirés des amplificateurs maison, elle déplace la Heston 120 du côté du meuble assumé plutôt que de l'électronique que l'on cherche à masquer. Les habitués de la marque y retrouveront la grammaire visuelle des Stanmore et autres Woburn, transposée cette fois sous le téléviseur. Un parti pris esthétique qui vaut autant que ses argume…

articles.title: Ahold Delhaize: Cyberattack affects services across US and Europe
articles.summary:
Ahold Delhaize, one of the world's largest food retail chains, confirmed that last week's cyberattack disrupted services at stores across Europe and the United States.
Right before the cyberattack was disclosed, customers couldn't use websites, apps, and customer service platforms at Albert Heijn, Etos, and Gall & Gall stores in the Netherlands, and Delhaize in Belgium, while employees at the Stop & Shop American regional supermarket chain reported having trouble accessing their schedules and pay stubs.
When BleepingComputer asked right after the incident whether it also affected both corporate and store systems and whether any devices were encrypted during the attack, an Ahold Delhaize spokesperson redirected us to the company's statement.
In a Monday update, Ahold Delhaize said the cybersecurity incident announced last week forced it to take some systems offline, including its brands' websites and apps, causing service issues, although stores remained open to serve customers.
While most store websites and apps in Central and Southeastern Europe (CSE) are now online, the company says it's still working to restore some systems and services for European and US brands that remain down.

articles.title: Inma y Jesús, españoles trabajando en Noruega: “Hemos ahorrado 10.000 € en tres meses; en España, con suerte, ahorrábamos 400 € al mes”
articles.summary:
Inma y Jesús se van a trabajar durante algún tiempo a Noruega para ahorrar dinero y poder seguir viajando por Asia. “Hemos ahorrado 10.000 euros en tres meses; en España, con suerte, ahorrábamos 400 euros al mes”, comentan sobre su experiencia. En España antes ejercían como trabajadores sociales.
Antes de marcharse, los dos probaron a cortar gastos para poder ahorrar cada mes algo más. “Pensábamos que el problema era que gastábamos mucho”, afirman. Dejar de salir con amigos y de comprar ropa les parecía una forma rápida de acumular ahorros, pero apenas consiguieron un incremento con el que quedar satisfechos.
El proceso para encontrar trabajo llevó varios meses hasta que lograron dar con una oportunidad en el extranjero para trabajar en Noruega durante la temporada de verano. Llegaron a dedicar “cinco o seis horas diarias” a buscar empleo. Además de ello, el trabajo que consiguieron es temporal.
Ahorrar para seguir viajando
El cálculo a partir de las cifras que da la pareja es sencillo. Si ahorraran 400 euros al mes, les llevaría 25 meses ahorrar 10.000 euros. Suponiendo, claro está, que consiguieran mantenerse ahorrando esa cantidad todos los meses, ya que era lo que podían guardar en España en el mejor de los casos.

articles.title: À 10 mètres sous l'eau, ces panneaux solaires ont réussi à recharger une batterie — Frandroid
articles.summary:
La lumière du soleil reste exploitable sous l’eau, même à 10 mètres de profondeur. C’est ce qu’ont montré des chercheurs de l’université du Yunnan, en Chine, associés notamment à l’EPFL de Lausanne, lors d’une expérience menée en conditions réelles en mer de Chine méridionale. Avec des cellules photovoltaïques immergées, ils ont produit assez d’électricité pour charger une batterie, qui a ensuite alimenté un panneau LED. Leurs travaux ont été publiés le 11 septembre dans la revue Joule.
Une cellule photovoltaïque adaptée aux longueurs d’onde sous-marines
Les panneaux solaires classiques sont mal adaptés à une utilisation sous-marine. Sous l’eau, le rouge et l’infrarouge sont vite absorbés, si bien que ces panneaux perdent une bonne partie de la lumière dont ils se servent sur terre. Pour tenir compte de ces conditions, les chercheurs ont développé une cellule photovoltaïque à base de pérovskite aux halogénures de plomb. Celle-ci convertit surtout la lumière bleue et verte, celle qui pénètre le plus loin dans l’eau, et son absorption est calée sur la lumière qui reste à 10 mètres de profondeur.
Les scientifiques ont également intégré à la pérovskite un polymère appelé chlorhydrate de polyhexaméthylène guanidine. Cet additif corrige des défauts du matériau et limite la migration des ions, ce qui améliore les performances de la cellule et sa stabilité dans le temps.
Calée sur la lumière bleue et verte, cette cellule n’est pas pensée pour remplacer les panneaux solaires classique…

articles.title: Star Wars Battlefront 3 en route chez Bungie (Halo) ?
articles.summary:
Neuf ans après le fiasco des lootbox de Battlefront II, qui avait poussé Disney à intervenir en coulisses auprès d’EA, l’engouement du public pour le jeu n’a paradoxalement jamais faibli. D’après EGM, les dirigeants de Lucasfilm déploient « activement des droïdes sondes » pour trouver un studio partenaire capable de relancer la série sans rejouer le fiasco de 2017. DICE et Bungie seraient dans le collimateur.
Le retour de DICE pour Star Wars Battlefront 3 ?
Le nom de DICE n’a rien d’une surprise : le studio suédois a développé les deux Battlefront d’EA, en 2015 et 2017, et maîtrise le moteur Frostbite comme les grandes batailles multijoueur. Celui de Bungie est beaucoup plus inattendu. Racheté par Sony en 2022, le studio connaît déjà Lucasfilm : les deux entreprises ont travaillé ensemble sur Destiny 2: Renegades, une extension inspirée de Star Wars, avec sabres laser et blasters, sortie le 2 décembre 2025. EGM ne dit pas si cette collaboration a pesé dans la balance.
Pour Lucasfilm, chaque option a ses atouts et ses risques. L’option DICE représente la facilité technique et la sécurité des ressources graphiques déjà existantes, à condition que le studio ait retenu les leçons du passé et ne soit pas totalement essoré par le développement de ses propres franchises.
L’option Bungie, ce sont des des sensations de tir reconnues et une longue expérience des jeux services, des jeux en ligne entretenus pendant des années, mais avec le risque de transformer Battlefront en jeu de tir …

articles.title: Trade Republic geht unter die Versicherer: Das steckt dahinter
articles.summary:
Trade Republic geht unter die Versicherer: Das steckt dahinter
Gerade erst ist Trade Republic mit einem kostenlosen Angebot in den Wettbewerb um das kommende Altersvorsorgedepot eingestiegen, da zeigt sich: Das Fintech hat für den staatlich geförderten Riester-Nachfolger wohl noch weitere Pläne.
Wie der Branchendienst “Versicherungsmonitor” als erster berichtete, hat der Berliner Neobroker unter dem Namen „Justinian Versicherungs AG“ einen eigenen Lebensversicherer gegründet. Damit wäre Trade Republic künftig auch in der Lage, eine Variante des Altersvorsorgedepots anzubieten, die eine Garantie-Komponente enthält.
Kampf um die besten Konditionen
Derzeit tobt ein Preiskampf um die Konditionen für die neue private Rentenvorsorge. Das Altersvorsorgedepot ist als Nachfolger der Riester-Rente geplant und soll Anfang 2027 starten. Der Staat steuert dann bis zu 540 Euro jährlich bei, wenn Sparer über Fonds, ETFs oder Anleihen fürs Alter vorsorgen.
Anbieter eines geförderten Altersvorsorgedepots müssen ein sogenanntes Standarddepot bereitstellen, bei dem die Effektivkosten maximal ein Prozent betragen dürfen. Das Geld wird dabei nach gesetzlichen Vorgaben auf einen Aktien- und einen Anleihen-Fonds verteilt.
Daneben bieten viele Broker auch eine günstige Variante für Selbstentscheider, bei der Kunden die Anlagen selbst aus einem Bündel von Aktien-, Anleihen- und Rohstoff-ETFs, Fonds oder ELTIFs auswählen können.
Einen gesetzlichen Kostendeckel gibt es hierfür nicht, aber aktuell werbe…

articles.title: J’ai testé l’Apple Watch Series 12 : elle corrige enfin ce qui m’agaçait depuis des années
articles.summary:
Réglée comme une horloge, Apple propose en cette rentrée sa nouvelle génération de montres connectées avec l’Apple Watch Series 12. Cette année, les nouveautés se cachent surtout sous le capot, avec une nouvelle puce et un capteur de fréquence cardiaque entièrement revu.

articles.title: AI Platform Cairn Abused to Hack Over 100 Organizations
articles.summary:
Threat actors have been abusing open source AI platform Cairn to automate malicious operations against hundreds of websites worldwide, AI security firm Norforge reports.
Cairn is a general-purpose problem-solving engine that can coordinate AI agents towards a set goal and can be used as an autonomous penetration testing engine.
Each task in Cairn is considered a project, with an origin and a predefined goal, and agents work step by step from origin to goal, posting their intents and findings to a shared blackboard.
Following a recent Gambit Security report on hackers using three AI harnesses to automate attacks against hundreds of online retailers, Norforge decided to investigate further and discovered that some threat actors left their panels open.
On Cairn, the cybersecurity firm identified three clusters of activity that appear to be malicious, focused on persistent access and financial theft.
The largest of the clusters uses Chinese language and comprises over 1,100 attack projects across 14 dashboards. It has targeted e-commerce/payment infrastructure in the US, Japan, and Australia.
According to Norforge, the threat actor’s goal appears to be persistent access to large platforms via webshells, likely to be monetized later. Automated validation was also included, and targets were ranked by traffic and tested using Microsoft’s browser automation framework Playwright before being fed to Cairn.

articles.title: Imágenes de la Pantera Rosa protestando en París no son reales, fueron hechas con IA
articles.summary:
La Pantera Rosa se convirtió en uno de los símbolos virales más comentados de las protestas en Francia, pero nunca pisó las calles de París. articles.title: Taking a swing at a pickleball startup
articles.summary:
Taking a swing at a pickleball startup
Stanley Anderson ’79
In corporate America, Stanley Anderson ’79 says, executives often assume that their peers grew up in privileged circumstances.
He did not.
“I spent my early years trying not to get recruited into gangs, getting shot at, watching my friends get murdered, and thinking that if I don’t leave, I will die,” says Anderson, who was raised in Chicago. “I was fortunate to survive.”
But he thrived, building an impressive career at the likes of HP, Intel, and the Palo Alto Research Center. Now he is applying his management expertise as CEO of Costa Pickleball, a Las Vegas–based startup that sells high-performance paddles in decorative designs. Beyond giving customers a way to, as he says, “bring their identity to the court,” he is also betting on technology: He’s developing a quieter type of paddle he expects will provide a competitive advantage.
Succeeding in today’s pickleball market will be tough, but Anderson thinks he has what it takes, partly thanks to an important lesson he learned at MIT: “There’s nothing you can’t accomplish if you are willing to put effort into it.”

Justin Mast’s life was changed by a cyborg plant.
A few years ago, Mast was reading through some scientific literature when he stumbled upon research about a houseplant wired to a motorized stand. When the plant wanted more light, electrical signals flowed through the living tissues. A control board sensed the current and wheeled the plant closer to the light source.
“I’m like, what the heck?” Mast told TechCrunch. “That was the entry to the rabbit hole for me.”
Mast wound up partnering with Lee von Kraus, a neuroscientist who has worked with DARPA, to found Electric Plant, which has been spending the past three years collecting data to build a large language model, Bombadil, capable of interpreting the subtle electrical signals coursing through a plant’s stem and relaying details about the plant’s needs to growers.
The founders believe their model could one day lead to a tool that would let people “speak” to plants. “We’re listening more than we’re speaking, but listening’s the first step,” said Mast, co-founder and CEO of Electric Plant.
To bring its sensors and Bombadil to market, Electric Plant recently raised an $11.2 million seed round led by Onto Ventures and Climactic, with participation from Ponderosa, Endeavor Catalyst, Ludlow, Michigan Rise, The Fund, Schox VC, and Dug Song.

articles.title: Robotic therapy for stroke patients
articles.summary:
Robotic therapy for stroke patients
An adaptive physical rehab system uses generative AI to learn from physical therapists and offer personalized support.
Strokes leave 5 million people with long-term impairments each year, and a growing shortage of physical therapists makes it hard for them to get the care they need. A new approach tries to solve that problem by combining artificial intelligence and human therapy.
Johannes Lachner, a former MIT postdoc who is now an assistant professor at Purdue University, and Noah Geiger, a former visiting student at MIT, developed a robotic system that uses generative AI and real-time force feedback to learn from real therapists. Drawing on what it’s learned, it gives patients just the right amount of assistance during physical rehabilitation exercises like reaching, lifting their arms, and performing tasks of daily living.
The goal is “not to replace therapists, but to extend their reach,” Lachner says.
“Initial robotic experiments have already demonstrated the feasibility of this approach,” he reports. “The next phase of the project aims to develop therapist-specific models and evaluate them in a long-term clinical study with the same patients who previously received manual therapy.” Beyond that, he envisions possible applications in contact-rich industrial settings or collaborative workspaces.

articles.title: Fine-tuning GPT-OSS-20B for multilingual reasoning on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Fine-tuning GPT-OSS-20B for multilingual reasoning on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod
GPT-OSS-20B is an open-weight reasoning model that thinks in English. Ask it to reason in French, German, Spanish, or Italian and it acknowledges the instruction, then produces its chain-of-thought in English anyway. On a 50-example multilingual reasoning test, the base model reasoned in the correct target language only 22 percent of the time. That 22 percent was almost entirely the English examples (English 100 percent, French 0 percent, German 10 percent, Spanish 0 percent, Italian 0 percent).
For teams deploying reasoning models for non-English users, that gap matters. A user who asks a question in French expects the model to reason and answer in French, not to switch to English mid-thought. Closing that gap is a fine-tuning problem. It raises a question every team faces once they start customizing open-weight models: supervised fine-tuning (SFT), reinforcement learning with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), or both?
In this post, we walk through how we fine-tuned GPT-OSS-20B for multilingual reasoning on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod. We show when SFT alone was sufficient and when GRPO added measurable value on top. To understand more broadly when GRPO helps, we also ran a controlled Qwen2.5-7B experiment across two tasks with different capability gaps. The short answer: SFT does most of the work, GRPO refines when there is headroom to refine, and matching the tech…

Beam is a new Mac app that takes a window running on one Mac and puts it on another, where it behaves like a locally installed app. Why? Agents.
Serial founder Hiten Shah, who co-founded Crazy Egg and KISSmetrics, built it with Sam Asante under a company called Noats. It launched on Product Hunt on Tuesday and is aimed at the headless Mac Mini sitting in a closet running AI agents.
The pitch is great: Instead of opening Screen Sharing and steering a full remote desktop, a user picks a single window on the other machine, say a Terminal session or a browser window an agent is working in, and it opens alongside everything else on the Mac in front of them. It gets its own Dock icon and can be called using the Command+Tab switcher. Resizing the window resizes the window on the other Mac. Keyboard shortcuts work, files can be dragged across, and the app’s audio can play locally. The app itself never leaves the original machine. When one window isn’t enough, Beam can pull over a full display or the whole Mac.
Shah frames it around his own setup in his Product Hunt launch post, describing Macs running agents and local models “with work continuing even when nobody’s sitting in front of them.” Getting to one of those machines usually means Screen Sharing and a second desktop to navigate. Beam is meant to cut that down to the one window that matters.

La fin de cette génération de téléphonie mobile s’était ensuite faite par vagues en métropole depuis le 31 mars, de Bayonne, Anglet et Biarritz jusqu’à 44 départements d’un coup le 6 octobre.

Pour Orange, la 2G, déployée dans les années 1990, « ne répond plus aux exigences actuelles en matière de connectivité ». Les fréquences occupées par cette norme vont être recyclées pour servir aux nouvelles générations que sont la 4G et la 5G. Orange avance aussi un argument énergétique en citant la Fédération française des télécoms : un gigaoctet transmis en 2G consomme jusqu’à 500 fois plus d’énergie qu’en 5G.
Quelques endroits garderont la 2G d’Orange un peu plus longtemps. À Mayotte, l’opérateur la coupera le 31 décembre. Quant aux zones blanches réglementaires, ces communes rurales où les opérateurs partagent les mêmes antennes, elles la perdront entre le 1er et le 15 décembre.

OVHcloud offers the CLI tool as an alternative for system administrators and developers to manage cloud and hosting services directly from a terminal, including for automating tasks.
OVHcloud CEO Octave Klaba disclosed that the company’s CLI repository on GitHub had been compromised, urging users who downloaded the latest version yesterday to update or remove the tool.
Klaba said that the compromised release appeared at 14:47 on October 19 and was detected and blocked at 16:21 after a customer reported it.
"The compromised versions are v0.11.0 v0.12.0 v0.13.0 v0.14.0 v0.15.0," the CEO said, adding that older version 0.10.0 and the latest release 0.16.0 were clean.
Despite the poor quality of the malware, its purpose was to "retrieve secrets from the disk," Klaba explained.
In a later update, Klaba shared that GitHub’s release immutability setting was disabled, allowing a sufficiently privileged account to modify existing releases without passing CI/CD checks.

Following last week’s announcement that Germany’s NEURA Robotics would be launching its multimodal foundation for physical AI, today the company confirmed that it would be working with Austria’s NXAI on a building block for the memory of cognitive robots.
To this end, the partners are combining NEURA’s Physical AI stack with xLSTM, a recurrent architecture from NXAI that can efficiently maintain and update state over long sequences. Furthermore, NXAI plans to make its own model, based on the xLSTM architecture, available on the Neuraverse platform.
It is set to be available alongside NEURA’s own foundation model, Neuron AI, in future.
“A robot that truly helps in everyday life and in industry must be able to remember,” says David Reger, founder and CEO of NEURA Robotics. “With Neuron AI, we have the foundation. With Neuraverse, we are creating the platform on which other powerful AI approaches can also find their way into robots. Together with Sepp Hochreiter and NXAI, we are expanding this memory capability. Two European strengths, one goal: Physical AI from Europe, together for the world.”
This follows a period of sustained growth for the Metzingen-based robotics unicorn.
As previously reported by EU-Startups, NEURA secured €15 million from InterAlpen Partners in 2023, following a €52 million round earlier that year. articles.title: Meta Muse exposes users' personal and business secrets when they share conversations
articles.summary:
Muse, the new general-purpose AI agent from Meta, can expose sensitive information when users share conversations through web links, researchers reported Monday. In response to questions from Ars about the behavior, Meta said it’s suspending the sharing feature while the company reviews it and considers making changes.
Like many online services, Muse has allowed users to share searches, conversations, images, and similar content with other people. Such share features usually involve clicking an option to create a unique URL that anyone can use to load a page hosting the content. To keep potentially sensitive information from being accessible to unintended people, the URLs typically contain a long sequence of text that can’t be easily guessed.
A single query is all that’s required
Muse, which Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said last month was “built from the ground up for privacy and security,” seems to take the same precautions. But a central design decision for constructing URLs has made the links easy to discover. As a result, researchers from security firm Claroc said they were able to enumerate 6,800 links Muse users created for sharing conversations with others. After opening a few hundred of them, the researchers found information that was clearly not intended to be publicly available, including:
- a candidate’s notes preparing for a confidential executive-search call with a frontier AI lab, naming the lab’s internal contact and the meeting time
- a national marketing company…

articles.title: Can a Simple App Really Fix PC Game Stutters?
articles.summary:
Shader compilation stutter has plagued PC gaming for years, and a new application called Shader Compilation Stutter Killer, or SCSKiller for short, promises to do something about it. The idea is simple enough: compile shaders before launching a game rather than waiting for them to be compiled during gameplay. But does it actually work?
That's what we set out to find out, testing the application across several notoriously stutter-prone games. Along the way, we also discovered something rather interesting about shader compilation on Radeon GPUs. Something that could be a pretty big deal, and that we hadn't heard about before.
What's SCSKiller?
SCSKiller is a free and open-source application, so if you're interested, we recommend downloading it and giving it a shot for yourself. For those unfamiliar with shader compilation stutter, it's a common issue in modern PC gaming where a game briefly freezes or hitches the first time a new visual effect appears.
Some games attempt to address this by precompiling shaders before gameplay begins. The Last of Us Part I, for example, is famous for its lengthy shader compilation process.
Unfortunately, even games that precompile shaders can still suffer from horrific shader compilation stutter, while others don't bother precompiling much of anything, which can also lead to a poor experience.
Rather than relying on a game to compile shaders, either beforehand or on the fly, SCSKiller attempts to do the work before you launch it. The application…

articles.title: Elon Musk y Anthropic discrepan sobre cómo repartir la riqueza generada por la IA
articles.summary:
Anthropic se ha comprometido a hacer todo lo que esté en su mano para atenuar el impacto que el desarrollo de la inteligencia artificial (IA) ya está teniendo en el mercado laboral. Este laboratorio estadounidense es uno de los más importantes de la industria de la IA, y, como os explicamos ayer, ha concretado su propuesta asegurando que va a destinar el 5% de sus acciones al Fondo de Beneficio Público, si lo aprueban sus accionistas.
Dario Amodei, el máximo responsable de Anthropic, ha declarado en varias ocasiones que la cada vez mayor penetración de la IA provocará que en menos de cinco años la mitad de los empleos de oficina de nivel inicial desaparezcan. Su tesis defiende que los modelos de IA podrán llevar a cabo esos trabajos con las máximas garantías, de modo que para las empresas será más rentable ceder esa responsabilidad a un modelo de lenguaje y prescindir de algunos de sus empleados.
Si observamos el ritmo al que ha evolucionado la IA durante los últimos seis meses, la previsión de cinco años de Amodei resulta incluso demasiado conservadora. Sea como sea, es evidente que es necesario abordar esta discusión y concretar cuál es la responsabilidad de los laboratorios de IA en el impacto que sus modelos ya están teniendo en el mercado laboral. Curiosamente, la perspectiva de Elon Musk es muy diferente al enfoque que ha puesto sobre la mesa Dario Amodei.

articles.title: Jusqu'à deux fois plus de tâches qu'Intel et AMD : le processeur ARM Nvidia Vera convainc un gros acteur — Frandroid
articles.summary:
Nvidia ne veut plus seulement vendre ses GPU, il veut aussi placer ses CPU dans les centres de données. Cela tombe bien puisque Nvidia a un client de plus pour son processeur Vera.
Dans un billet de blog publié ce lundi 19 octobre, Modal annonce qu’elle va faire tourner une partie de ses services sur ce CPU. Cette start-up américaine loue de la puissance de calcul aux développeurs d’IA.
Ses serveurs n’utilisaient jusqu’ici que des puces x86 d’Intel et AMD. Nvidia domine déjà le marché des GPU pour l’IA, et la voilà qui prend pied sur le terrain historique de ses deux concurrents.
Modal pèse déjà lourd dans le secteur. La société a levé 750 millions de dollars (environ 670 millions d’euros) le 14 octobre, pour une valorisation de 15,75 milliards de dollars (environ 14 milliards d’euros), et vise le milliard de dollars de chiffre d’affaires sur un an. Vera servira à son produit Sandboxes. Ce sont des environnements isolés où les agents IA (ces programmes qui enchaînent seuls des tâches longues, comme écrire et tester du code) exécutent leurs commandes.
Deux fois plus de tâches, mais sous forte charge
Pour comparer les puces, Modal a construit son propre test, baptisé Agentless Agent Bench. Il fait tourner 50 tâches typiques d’un agent (compiler du code, fouiller des fichiers, manipuler un dépôt Git) dans des conteneurs Docker lancés en parallèle, sans appel réseau. Face à Vera, on trouve des serveurs Intel Granite Rapids, AMD Zen 5 et AWS Graviton 4 et 5.

articles.title: Des hackers détournent des serveurs Plex non mis à jour pour miner des cryptos, le vôtre est-il en danger ?
articles.summary:
Plus de deux mois après la publication des correctifs, des pirates exploitent plusieurs failles de Plex Media Server. Les machines compromises servent à miner des cryptomonnaies, mais aussi à relayer du trafic Internet à l'insu de leurs propriétaires.
Début septembre, Plex appelait une nouvelle fois ses utilisateurs et utilisatrices à installer une mise à jour de sécurité sur leurs serveurs multimédias. Si l'éditeur se montrait discret sur la nature des vulnérabilités corrigées, il ne faisait alors état d'aucune exploitation active. C'est désormais chose faite depuis la publication, le 16 octobre dernier, d'un code permettant d'exploiter quatre de ces failles pour exécuter du code à distance sur un serveur, sans authentification. Dès le lendemain, un chercheur observait des tentatives d'intrusion sur un serveur leurre, tandis que des propriétaires d'installations non patchées signalaient à leur tour des activités suspectes.
Plex2Shell, quatre vulnérabilités exploitées en chaîne
Baptisée Plex2Shell, cette méthode d'attaque repose sur l'enchaînement de quatre vulnérabilités, référencées CVE-2026-96652, CVE-2026-96654, CVE-2026-96655 et CVE-2026-96656. Leur exploitation combinée permet de contourner les contrôles d'accès de Plex, de récupérer le jeton d'administration du serveur, puis d'y déposer un fichier malveillant que le logiciel exécutera avec les privilèges du processus Media Server.

articles.title: A reason to eat carbs
articles.summary:
A reason to eat carbs
MIT researchers have found that a ketogenic diet may fuel the growth of some intestinal tumors.
A high-fat, low-carbohydrate diet can help some people lose weight, and some research has shown that it may protect against colon cancer. But a new study suggests that such a ketogenic diet may also increase the risk of cancer in the small intestine.
This type of diet forces the body to burn fatty acids instead of carbohydrates for fuel, producing by-products called ketone bodies. One of these, BHB, was thought to be responsible for the protective effect observed against colon cancer.
Omer Yilmaz, director of the MIT Stem Cell Initiative, worked with colleagues including MIT postdocs Jessica Shay and Fangtao Chi to investigate whether the effects were similar in the small intestine. But instead, they found that mice on a ketogenic diet were more likely to develop tumors in that part of the gastrointestinal system than those on a control diet were.
Additional studies revealed that this tumor growth was driven by the way intestinal cells burn dietary fat for energy—a metabolic pathway called fatty acid oxidation. This pathway activates proteins that signal stem cells to multiply more rapidly.
“Having more stem cells means that when you injure the small intestine, it can repair itself better, but the downside is that having more active stem cells can lead to tumor formation,” Yilmaz says.

articles.title: Streaming guide JustWatch becomes a streamer itself | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
JustWatch, a company offering a search engine and guide for streaming movies and TV shows, is now moving directly into the streaming business itself. On Tuesday, the company behind the popular guide that’s used by 50 million people is launching JustWatch TV. The new streaming service will feature content from 30 partners and will offer both free and paid tiers, as well as a movie rental store.
The media and entertainment company behind the streaming guide, the JustWatch Group, initially announced its plans to venture into streaming last month. At the time, it said partners like Paramount, New Regency, Fremantle, Bleecker Street, and Vortex Media were on board. The company has since announced other content partners, including Cineverse in the U.S., LEONINE Studios in Germany, SND in France, and Altitude in the U.K.
The 12-year-old company has long been known for its online guide to movies and TV. Essentially, it’s a “TV Guide” for the streaming era, helping users navigate a landscape where movies and shows move from one service to another, making it harder to keep up with what’s streaming where.
Available in 140 markets globally, the guide provides streaming options for more than 500,000 movies and shows across more than 1,500 service providers worldwide. articles.title: The Key to AI Software Security Isn’t Speed, It’s Maturity
articles.summary:
Agentic artificial intelligence software development has all the traits of a summer blockbuster, with the prospects of Godzilla-sized productivity gains thrilling business leaders and security implications sending chills down the spines of developers and SOC teams. One difference, though, is that those thrills and chills are going to last longer than a summer, and the fallout could be a lot more serious than some spilled popcorn.
The proliferation of large language models, whether for software development or general use, alongside both sanctioned tools and shadow AI brought in by employees, is expanding the attack surface too quickly for traditional controls to keep up, particularly with the growing use of agentic AI. And the increased risks are coming home to roost, with Gartner predicting that the costs of incidents driven by agentic AI will increase fourfold through 2027.
The impact of agentic AI is a particularly sharp double-edged sword, with SonarSource noting that the frontier LLMs such as Claude and Gemini that write the best, most functional code also produce the most severe security vulnerabilities.
Organizations are aware of the need to gain control over agentic AI’s risk factors, but the protections implemented so far may well be insufficient. Governance is the go-to concept for reigning in AI-driven software development, and with good reason. It’s critical for maintaining control over what AI agents can and can’t do. articles.title: Polestar tries to quantify what it’s like to drive a performance car
articles.summary:
The human desire to go fast is old, dating back at least as far as the first time some adventurous Yamnaya saw a horse on the Pontic-Caspian steppe and thought, “I bet if I jumped on that thing’s back, it would be faster than walking.”
A thousand years later, someone else invented the wheel—and the chariot—and humanity was ready to roll. Now, about five millennia since that first horseback ride, equestrianism is mostly a leisure activity, and we drive cars, propelled by motors with more power than an entire herd of beasts could muster.
Acceleration, top speed, and lap times are the usual ways we quantify that performance, and performance electric vehicles are currently in an arms race to see which one can hit 60 mph in the least amount of time. But measuring a car’s performance is easy—all you need is a stopwatch and a track. How about measuring the effect of car performance on the driver? That’s a question Polestar is trying to answer with researchers at the University of Oxford.
“As electric cars redefine what performance can be, we wanted to understand something that can’t be captured by a specification sheet alone: the human experience behind the wheel,” said Christian Samson, Polestar’s head of product attributes. “Working with University of Oxford allows us to look at performance through a different lens—connecting the engineering of the car with the experience of the person driving it.”

In a nutshell: A lot of people cite the 1990s Nokia 3210 as the old-school brick-like mobile phone. But for something that fits the description a lot closer, go back another decade to the 1980's and the first handheld mobile phones: brick phones. Now, a designer has 3D-printed one of these devices, retaining the originals' primary function of making and receiving calls – so there are no modern smartphone distractions.
Cologne-based designer and maker Kevin Noki created the ADHD ONE, the first part of the name being an acronym for Anti Distraction Handset Device.
The device resembles a snazzy update of 1980s brick phones sported by the likes of Wall Street's Gordon Gekko, such as the Motorola DynaTAC 8000X. There's the physical 19-key keypad, small display, and a concerning large antenna.
The phone has a much more modern set of internals. It's powered by a Raspberry Pi Pico and features an FSC-BT1026C Bluetooth module based on Qualcomm's QCC3024 chip. There's also a rechargeable lithium battery, charging controller, and custom-printed circuit board.
Unlike the 1980s originals, the ADHD ONE doesn't have its own cellular connectivity. Instead, it relies on a Bluetooth connection to an iPhone to make and receive calls, so it's not like you can completely replace your distraction-filled smartphone with one of these, but you can at least keep it hidden in a drawer.
Noki designed the phone's enclosure using Autodesk Fusion before 3D-printing the components. He's made the files avail…

Launched on October 7, 2026, the NCC’s Device Checker requires consumers to dial *315# to verify whether a phone meets Type Approval requirements—the NCC’s mandatory regulation that all communication equipment must meet before connecting to local networks.

The checker uses a phone’s International Mobile Equipment Identity (IMEI), a unique 15-digit identifier, to verify its status against the NCC’s approved equipment records. articles.title: Windows Server 2025 gets support for quick machine recovery
articles.summary:
Microsoft announced that IT administrators can now use quick machine recovery on Windows Server 2025 after installing the October 2026 security update.
Quick machine recovery (QMR) lets IT admins fix critical boot failures with targeted Windows Update fixes without physical access to affected systems.
When enabled, it boots into the Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE) and launches the QMR Tool if Windows 11 fails to start because of a configuration change or a new driver. It then sends crash data to Microsoft, which can remotely fix issues by adjusting settings or removing problematic drivers or updates.
"With the October 2026 security update, quick machine recovery extends to Windows Server 2025," the company said in a message center update.
"Quick machine recovery is designed to help restore devices experiencing widespread boot issues by using the Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE) to search Windows Update for applicable remediations."
On Windows Server 2025, cloud remediation is disabled by default, but admins can enable it via Group Policy under Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > System > Quick Machine Recovery to retrieve and apply cloud-sourced remediation.
For local configuration, admins must sign in to the target server with administrator permissions and use the Local Group Policy Editor. articles.title: OPINION: Europe needs more than just successful exits | EU-Startups

The acquisition of Berlin-based Talon.One by Dutch payments provider Adyen in July 2026 offers a useful perspective on European technology investing. A company founded in Germany developed technology valuable to a global payments business, and its next chapter is being written within Europe. This is a significant outcome for the founders and investors. However, it also raises a larger question: how can Europe turn individual successes into an ecosystem capable of producing them repeatedly?
The answer is not simply to encourage more European acquisitions. Successful startups need access to the best opportunities available, whether their future lies with a European buyer, an international technology group or the public markets. What matters is that these decisions reflect commercial potential rather than a lack of viable alternatives. For Europe, the challenge is to create the conditions in which successful companies can scale, attract investment and generate lasting economic value.
Exits are a measure of maturity, not the final destination
From a venture capital perspective, exits matter because they return capital to investors and founders, establish reference points for valuations, and help to finance the next generation of start-ups. From data to decisions: Conversational supply chain intelligence with Amazon Quick and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
Giving supply chain teams direct access to the systems behind their decisions.

Answering “which top-revenue SKUs are exposed to the current port closure, and what will it cost?” used to mean knowing which system held each piece and stitching them together by hand while the domain expert waited.

articles.title: Melt it, spin it, use it again
articles.summary:
Melt it, spin it, use it again
A plastic-based recyclable yarn is as strong and stretchy as spandex.
The average American throws out around 81 pounds of clothing each year, and there are few options for recycling it. MIT engineers hope to cut down on that textile waste with a new type of yarn.
The thermoplastic yarn mimics the properties of conventional elastic yarns, which typically combine spandex with polyester or nylon. Those fibers would have to be separated for recycling—a process that isn’t practical. But the MIT team found a way to create a similarly stretchy yarn from two variations of polyethylene, a material commonly used in milk jugs and grocery bags. Because they come from the same chemical family, the yarn can be melted as is. Svetlana Boriskina, who led the work as a research scientist in the Department of Mechanical Engineering, says a garment made from this material could then be spun into new yarn for a next generation of clothing. Even after 10 cycles of melting and respinning, the yarn stays as strong and flexible as conventional thread.
“Now we have something that can be knitted and woven,” Boriskina says. “That is the next stage.” Someday, the researchers hope, a polyethylene garment could be dropped in a collection bin and sent to a recycling facility, promoting a more sustainable, circular textile economy.

articles.title: Quantum error correction goes well beyond breakeven
articles.summary:
Running complicated algorithms on quantum computing hardware is going to require the use of logical qubits, where collections of hardware qubits are linked together in ways that allow errors to be detected and corrected. In general, the more hardware qubits you dedicate to each logical qubit, the better the chances are of identifying errors. But, given that the hardware qubits are prone to errors, adding more of them also increases the probability that errors will occur. If the hardware error rate is too high, then growing the logical qubit will only make matters worse.
Fortunately, several companies have demonstrated hardware where the error rate is not too high. Several demonstrations show logical qubits are beyond the breakeven point, where adding more qubits improves performance. The problem is that the improvement isn’t very dramatic. To lower error rates to levels we’ll need to run complex algorithms, we’d have to add a completely impractical number of qubits to each logical qubit.
On Monday, Quantinuum announced that its current generation of hardware is capable of scaling well beyond the breakeven point. Each step up in the size of logical qubits improved some measures of their performance by a factor of over 10.

articles.title: Beyond the KV cache: Training and serving i14’s Laplace 3B linear attention model on AWS Trainium2 with native PyTorch | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Beyond the KV cache: Training and serving i14’s Laplace 3B linear attention model on AWS Trainium2 with native PyTorch
Most large language models (LLMs) use transformer architectures with softmax attention. During inference, their key-value (KV) cache grows with the conversation or document context. This can reduce concurrency, increase serving cost, and force agentic applications to discard useful history.
i14 designed Laplace 3B as a linear attention alternative. Its recurrent state stays at 29.5 MB per sequence, independent of context length. Working with AWS, i14 used native PyTorch support through TorchNeuron Native to bring this custom architecture to AWS Trainium2. This preserved its Gated Linear Attention (GLA) design and Muon optimizer.
On one trn2.48xlarge instance, Laplace 3B trained at about 120,000 tokens per second. The model served 11,544 output tokens per second across 1,280 concurrent sequences. This post explains the model design, the changes i14 made for Trainium2, and the training and inference results.
About i14
i14 is an AI research and technology company that develops model architectures, components, and runtimes. Its work draws on AI, computational cognitive science, and research into how biological systems learn over time. i14 applies these ideas to models that can retain long-range context without allowing serving state to grow with every token.

AI review took over bug-finding. But it didn’t take over the conversation where a team debates what it decided and why, and that is the part I missed too.
The part AI review doesn’t solve
Most teams are stuck in one of two modes. They review every line and become the bottleneck, or they rubber-stamp and lose track of what changed and why. There is no middle ground yet.
“The argument over whether engineers should stop reading code is over, because we already have.”
AI review is good at the mechanical half of the job. It never gets tired, it reads every line, and it holds the same standard on every PR. But it never saw what was decided. It won’t tell you not to build something, and it can’t be accountable for the result. A better model won’t fix that, because the tool reads the wrong artifact at the wrong time.
As I wrote in “Kill the code review theater, keep the review,” code review is how a team builds a mental model of its system. That has been the only scheduled moment for engineers to talk to each other about that system. Teams that hand code reviews to AI tools rarely notice they’ve also given up that moment.

articles.title: Data centre vs Cloud platform: Is there a difference?
articles.summary:
You have probably seen the words “data centre” and “cloud” used interchangeably. They don’t mean the same thing, and the difference matters. It shapes how businesses buy technology, how regulators write rules and where investors see opportunity.
A data centre is a building. It is a secure, purpose-built facility with reliable power, cooling, security and internet connections, so that computers can run around the clock. A cloud platform is a service. It is software that lets customers rent computing power, storage, and networking on demand, switch them on or off themselves, and pay only for what they use.
Think of an airport and an airline. The airport provides the runway, fuel, and terminal; the airline provides the service you actually book. Every cloud platform runs inside a data centre, but most data centres do not offer a cloud platform. Owning an airport does not make you an airline.
Data centre grading and cloud computing standards
Companies that rent space for their own servers in someone else’s facility are buying what the industry calls “colocation”. A facility’s reliability is rated on a four-level scale from the Uptime Institute.
Tier I has no backup equipment, so any fault results in downtime. Tier II adds spares but has a single path for power and cooling.
Tier III has more than one path, so any part can be serviced without switching anything off; it is the level most serious operators aim for. Tier IV survives any single failure.
