articles.title: Après les violents pillages, pourquoi l’état d’urgence ne permettrait pas de bloquer les réseaux sociaux
articles.summary:
Après les pillages du 17 octobre, certains, comme Bruno Retailleau, réclame l’état d’urgence et le gouvernement le garde en réserve. Ce régime d’exception issu d’une loi de 1955 permettrait surtout des mesures individuelles, mais pas de couper librement les réseaux sociaux.
Depuis les pillages qui ont suivi les manifestations du 17 octobre, l'état d'urgence s'est invité dans de nombreuses conversations, des plateaux télé aux fils d'actualité, aussi bien c'est ceux qui réclament son instauration que ceux qui le vilipendent. Le gouvernement de Sébastien Lecornu a préféré miser lundi soir des couvre-feux localisés à Paris, Lyon ou Lille, tout en gardant le régime d'exception sous le coude « si c'est nécessaire ». Entre la loi de 1955, la jurisprudence du Conseil d’État sur TikTok et le règlement européen DSA sur le services numériques, les marges de manœuvre de l’exécutif sont pourtant plus étroites qu’il n’y paraît.
L'état d’urgence, un pouvoir d’exception, pas un chèque en blanc
Cette fameuse loi de 1955, justement, mérite qu'on s'y arrête. Votée le 3 avril 1955, en pleine guerre d'Algérie, elle a donné naissance à un régime d'exception que la Constitution ne mentionne même pas, et qui ne peut être déclenché qu'en cas de péril imminent lié à des atteintes graves à l'ordre public. Le président le décrète en conseil des ministres, pour douze jours maximum. Au-delà, seul le Parlement peut le prolonger par une loi, qui devient caduque quinze jours après une démission du gouverneme…

Physical AI brings AI into machines that must sense their surroundings, make decisions, and act in the physical world. The market opportunity is substantial: McKinsey estimates that AI-powered agents and robots could unlock about $2.9 trillion in annual economic value in the U.S. by 2030. However, realizing this opportunity depends on moving from working prototypes to products that can operate reliably, safely, and economically at scale.
That exposes a different engineering problem. In a prototype, teams can often add more compute, sensors, cooling, or power to prove that a capability works. In deployment, every added capability must fit within the size, weight, power, and cost budget, often abbreviated to SWaP-C, of the system.
Those constraints shape how a robot performs: How long it can operate between charges, how much productive payload it can carry, and how reliably it operates over time. The challenge is not simply adding more intelligence but integrating it effectively into deployable products.
A robot must continuously interpret its surroundings, decide how to respond, and translate those decisions into physical action. Doing that requires capabilities from perception and AI inference to planning and motion control to work together, while meeting different compute and timing requirements.

In experiments carried out in a water tank and at Lake Geneva, a team led by Raphael Zufferey, an assistant professor of mechanical engineering at MIT, identified combinations of wing size, flapping frequency, and tail angle that enable the robot to smoothly transition from swimming to flying.

These robots move chips between tools and sections of the fab.
Intel has asked the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to make an exception for the automated guided vehicles (AGVs) that the company uses to transport the sensitive silicon wafers and other materials, containers, and supplies needed to make the most advanced chips in its fabs. articles.title: The cash cost of a 60-day customer (Sponsored) | EU-Startups

A bigger UK contract can consume runway before it creates cash. Put the payment terms into the funding plan before signing.
A large UK customer offers a scale-up a contract with 60-day payment terms. The revenue looks attractive. The less visible question is how much cash the startup must find before the customer pays.
Before signing, put the collection date into the cash forecast and compare it with when wages, suppliers and taxes must be paid. Then test what happens if payment takes longer. A profitable contract can still need funding, and a revenue target does not supply it.
This matters particularly for founders selling services or software to larger organizations. The customer may have enough money to pay. It may also have a procurement process that requires a purchase order, an approved invoice and a particular payment run. Winning the account and financing the account are different jobs.

At 30 days from invoicing to cash, average receivables would be roughly £395,000. At 60 days, they would be about £789,000. The extra 30 days ties up approximately £395,000 in invoices, without adding a pound of annual revenue.

articles.title: Scripted tests can't keep up with AI-written code. Datadog is betting agents can.

Scripted tests can’t keep up with AI-written code. Datadog is betting agents can.
Nearly a year into the agentic coding explosion, many teams now use AI to write software as their de facto approach. As a result, Anthropic’s engineers are shipping eight times as much code as before, and some engineers are shipping thousands of PRs per month.
Management teams expecting their engineering capacity to explode will find that AI-written code doesn’t necessarily compress the software development lifecycle (SDLC) on its own.
The critical bottleneck in software creation has shifted from writing code to a later SDLC stage. After coding agents spit out new code, it still needs testing, and traditionally that meant humans writing the tests. That work includes deciding which user flows need testing, scripting tests for them, and rejiggering them when those flows change.
We’ve made it easy to write code and, in the process, increased the burden on humans to test new code. If we want to slash software development timelines, something has to change.
The observability and monitoring giant Datadog bought Propolis earlier this year, adding agent-written, goal- and output-oriented test writing to its platform. The approach lets agents explore applications, follow user flows on their own, and generate tests from plain-language prompts.

Multi-Factor Authentication
CJIS v6.1 requires MFA for both privileged and non-privileged accounts under controls IA-2(1) and IA-2(2), covering local, network, and remote access. The challenge is making sure no accounts slip through the cracks.
Start by reviewing MFA coverage across your environment, paying particular attention to legacy applications and administrative accounts. When implementing MFA, consider phishing-resistant methods such as FIDO2 security keys.

articles.title: Does anyone actually want to win the medium-lift race in the United States?
articles.summary:
It has been 13 years since the debut of a new medium-lift rocket in the United States, the Antares vehicle developed by Orbital Sciences Corporation.
The initial 100-series variant of the Antares rocket was kind of a hot mess. The rocket used old Soviet engines built during the era when Apollo astronauts were landing on the Moon. Decades later, in the 1990s, Aerojet acquired the engines and refurbished them for a rocket that would launch in the 2010s. Predictably, on the fifth launch of an Antares rocket in 2014, it exploded.
The Antares vehicle is the last of a dying breed of medium-lift rockets—defined as having a lift capacity of 2 to 20 metric tons—in the United States. Nearly a decade and a half later there is a new generation of medium-lift vehicles coming online, and they are starkly different from Antares, which had not just Russian engines but a core stage manufactured in Ukraine.
Four forthcoming rockets all have engines built by the rocket’s manufacturer in the United States. Each of these companies has taken various lessons from SpaceX’s successful Falcon 9 rocket, arguably the most important of which is to build as much of one’s rocket, and particularly the engines, in-house as possible to control timelines and costs.

articles.title: Marie Curie y Einstein se escribieron cartas durante más de 20 años. 100 años después podemos leer lo que se decían
articles.summary:
El 7 de julio de 1922, Marie Curie le escribió a Albert Einstein para echarle la bronca. Con buenas formas, sí; pero bronca al fin y al cabo: Curie le llegaba a decir que le había causado una 'gran decepción'.
Durante 21 años, dos de los científicos más importantes de la historia se escribieron cartas en las que apenas se hablaba de física. Lo que hicieron fue cubrirse las espaldas. Y ahora, un siglo después, podemos leer la historia completa.
¿"Una gran decepción"? Tres días antes de aquella carta del 7 de julio, Einstein le había contado a Curie que iba a dimitir de la comisión de cooperación intelectual de la Sociedad de Naciones. Le confesó las razones, pero le pidió que no se las contara a nadie.
El 24 de junio habían asesinado en Berlín al ministro de Exteriores de la República de Weimar, Walther Rathenau, un viejo amigo de Einstein. Aquello había acabado por desmoralizarle. Y, precisamente por eso, Curie le cantaba las cuarenta. Claro que había corrientes de opinión extremadamente dañinas, pero a su juicio había que combatirlas y, de hecho, estaba convencida de que el mismo Rathenau estaría de acuerdo con ella. ¿No había alguna posibilidad de que cambiara de idea?
Un libro para la historia de la ciencia. No ha sido fácil recopilar la correspondencia entre ambos. Durante años, se han rastreado archivos en Jerusalén, París, Zúrich, Princeton, Düsseldorf o Varsovia y apenas se han encontrado 32 cartas. articles.title: Cuáles son las cinco prácticas que hacen que la computadora dure menos de uno o dos años
articles.summary:
Muchos usuarios creen que un computador se vuelve lento o se avería por simple antigüedad, pero en la mayoría de los casos el desgaste prematuro responde a hábitos cotidianos que pasan desapercibidos.
Desde bloquear la ventilación hasta instalar programas sin control, existen prácticas que deterioran tanto el hardware como el software del equipo, y que son evitables con cuidados básicos.
Hábitos que afectan el tiempo de vida de un computador
- Bloquear la ventilación y acumular polvo
El calor es el principal enemigo de cualquier equipo. Los ventiladores integrados en la carcasa cumplen la función de ingresar aire fresco y expulsar el calor interno, un proceso que se ve comprometido cuando se usa el portátil sobre superficies blandas, como una cama, un sillón o las piernas.
El polvo y las pelusas que se acumulan en las entradas de aire también atascan el interior y empeoran la circulación. Esto genera un recalentamiento progresivo que puede dañar los componentes.
Por eso conviene usar el equipo siempre sobre una mesa rígida, limpiar los puertos externos cada mes y abrir el chasis cada tres meses para eliminar el polvo interior con aire comprimido.
- Dejar que el equipo se sobrecaliente
Cada componente de un computador está diseñado para funcionar dentro de un rango de temperatura específico. Superarlo acelera su degradación o provoca averías directas.
Un exceso de calor puede derretir soldaduras y desplazar componentes, además de secar la pasta térmica de la CPU, lo que reduce…

Le 15 octobre 2026, l’agence spatiale a attiré l’attention sur ses observations par satellite du phénomène, qui s’annonce comme l’un des plus intenses depuis des décennies.
La Nasa confirme ainsi ce qu’annoncent les agences météorologiques depuis le printemps. Depuis juin 2026, le phénomène climatique El Niño a officiellement commencé. Selon l’Organisation météorologique mondiale (OMM), El Niño devrait se maintenir jusqu’en février 2027. Désormais, c’est la Nasa qui indique que ses satellites détectent des signes d’un épisode d’El Niño potentiellement « historique » cet automne.
El Niño revient environ tous les 2 à 7 ans, rappelle la Nasa, mais l’épisode de 2026 sort du lot par son intensité. En octobre, l’Agence américaine d’observation océanique et atmosphérique (NOAA) estimait à 83 % la probabilité qu’il s’agisse du plus fort El Niño depuis 1950.

El Niño est une composante d’un phénomène climatique naturel, El Niño-oscillation australe (ENSO). L’ENSO correspond à des variations des températures de surface de l’océan, dans le centre et l’est du Pacifique. El Niño en est la phase chaude, La Niña la phase froide, et le troisième état est appelé « ENSO neutre ».

Odiar el verano. Antes de entrar en el porqué ocurre esto a los amantes de la lluvia, hay que desmentir el hecho de que a todo el mundo le afecte el clima de la misma manera. Aunque curiosamente, se desmitifica la idea de la "relajación profunda" bajo la lluvia, puesto que la falta de luz solar se asociaba directamente con un mayor cansancio.

Foveated imaging is nothing new; it's a technique that's been used in VR to increase performance. It works by only rendering what's in view, often increasing the resolution in the center and reducing it at the edges. Our eyes work in a similar way, with the clearest image in a small area in the center of your vision, blurring on the edges. With foveated rendering, you barely notice the lower-resolution edges as the peripheral vision is less concerned with fine details.
Instead of varying the resolution of the image, however, it varies the level of detail in DLSS 5 Neural Rendering. DLSS NR loads a whole AI model into your GPU and renders images in real time, making it a resource-intensive task; but the task is minimized greatly when most of the detail is only asked for in the middle of the image. articles.title: The Internet goes on high alert after discovery of 8 compromised TLS certs

Security personnel around the world are on high alert Tuesday following the discovery of eight TLS certificates with private keys so weak they could allow anyone to mint trusted browser and app credentials for any site on the Internet.
As of late morning Tuesday, browser makers and some major apps and programming languages had blocked all eight of the intermediate certificates. There are no reports of certificate transparency logs, which track the issuance of all browser-trusted certificates, showing the compromised keys being used maliciously. The threat remains far from over, however, because it will be hard and time-consuming to update other key parts of the Internet, such as Linux distributions and embedded and Internet of Things devices.
One word: bonkers
The eight intermediate certificates belong to India-based certificate authority eMudhra Limited. An informal advisory published to emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com over on Tuesday posted the message “We have a problem here – Wayne.” The words were digitally signed using the private key of one of the eMudhra certificates. With proof that the reporting party had control of the key, defenders scrambled because the same key could be used to sign unauthorized certificates that would be trusted by millions of servers worldwide.

articles.title: Agents are breaking AI economics, and the fix starts in the data layer - SiliconANGLE

Agents are breaking AI economics, and the fix starts in the data layer
When companies talk about the cost of artificial intelligence, the conversation almost always starts with models: which one to use, what it costs per million tokens, and whether a smaller model is “good enough.” That made sense when AI meant a chatbot.
It makes much less sense now that agents are doing real work in production. A single agent task can fire off dozens of queries, pull context from several systems, call a model several times and write results back. What a task costs and how fast it runs are increasingly determined by everything that happens around the model.
During a pre-briefing ahead of this week’s expansion of the company’s AI Data Plane, Tim Finley, Couchbase Inc.‘s senior vice president of AI, highlighted a key trend. The company announced native Amazon Bedrock integration with semantic caching, a fully managed Agent Memory and Model Context Protocol server on Amazon Web Services, and vector search in its analytics engine, now called Operational Insights.
The more interesting part is the reasoning behind the release, which points to a problem most information technology leaders haven’t fully accounted for.
Agents are a different kind of user

articles.title: Un pájaro diminuto revoluciona Mieres: la aparición de una curruca gavilana, vista solo 14 veces en España, desata una peregrinación ornitológica
articles.summary:
Si usted no es ornitólogo, la frase “curruca gavilana en Mieres” quizá no le diga absolutamente nada. Para quienes miramos pájaros, equivale a ver un cometa desde el balcón. Pero mejor hagamos un examen a vista de pájaro, para no confundir plumaje. Solo adelanto un detalle: tirarles fotos a estas aves es esencial, pero si lo hacen un puñado de aficionados con carísimos teleobjetivos, es normal que cualquiera que lo vea por la calle piense que son unos ladinos paparazzi intentando cazar a la influencer de turno.
Qué pasó. El 12 de octubre, Clemente Álvarez Usategui, responsable de la Coordinadora Ornitológica de Asturias, paseaba por el parque Aníbal Vázquez, en La Mayacina, como hace casi a diario desde finales de julio. Había notado que el parque funcionaba como corredor para aves migratorias, así que iba cada día.
Esa mañana, entre los arbustos, fotografió una curruca gavilana. Según contó él mismo, es la cuarta vez que se ve en Asturias y la número 14 en España. Los registros públicos de observación sitúan al ave en el parque el 12 y el 13 de octubre, y un observador la calificó de una de las rarezas del otoño asturiano.
Quién es. Mide 15,5 centímetros y alcanza entre 23 y 27 de envergadura. Diminuta comparado con una paloma, enorme para una curruca (porque pesa entre 26 y 30 gramos). Assess the entire inference stack — not just open model benchmarks
Impressive benchmark results should make it easy for engineers to select the right open model for the outcome they are tasked with developing. However, that is not the case.
Benchmarks indicate an open model’s optimal performance, but in production, a model must work repeatedly. The challenge is that in production, other factors matter, such as the information provided to the model and its accuracy. So benchmarks can’t tell an engineer whether the AI they are developing will complete the task accurately, or even at all. This is especially important for long-horizon AI tasks.
Ryan Hanrui Wang, SVP of Applied AI at AI cloud provider Nebius, tells The New Stack it is important to measure an open model by the industry benchmarks in conjunction with internal benchmarks and harnesses to ensure you get the inference outcomes the organization requires, something he says the Amsterdam, Netherlands-based company always does in partnership with its clients.
Wang joined Nebius when it acquired Eigen AI, the inference-optimization startup he co-founded and led as CEO, in a roughly $643 million deal announced in May; Nebius sells inference through its Token Factory platform.

On Tuesday, Google announced that TorchTPU, its long-awaited version of PyTorch, is now available as an open source project. With this, Google joins Amazon in trying to break Nvidia’s stranglehold on the AI industry, where most AI apps are written by default to run on Nvidia’s chips, or GPUs.
PyTorch is the popular open source toolkit that AI app developers and startups use to build, train, and run AI models. It is, by some accounts, used by 85% of the AI apps. PyTorch was originally developed by Meta (then Facebook) in 2016, long before the world had an inkling that LLMs would change the world. At the time, Nvidia’s GPUs were already the standard hardware for AI research, so many of PyTorch’s features were built to work specifically with them. In 2022, Meta turned PyTorch over to the Linux Foundation, a nonprofit that manages many important open source projects.
Google’s version, TorchTPU, lets AI apps run on Google’s AI chips, called Tensor Processing Units (TPUs). It also makes it easy to move existing PyTorch apps to TPUs and, therefore, to Google Cloud. Developers can do this with a simple configuration change and no rewriting of their apps.
Amazon made a similar announcement Monday, when it released its own version of PyTorch, called TorchNeuron. TorchNeuron allows AI apps to be ported to Amazon’s homegrown AI chip, Trainium, and to AWS with no rewriting. GitHub has released Actions Runner Controller (ARC) 0.15.0, introducing reliability, scalability, and observability improvements for organisations running self-hosted GitHub Actions runners on Kubernetes. ARC is a Kubernetes operator that automatically scales self-hosted runners in response to workflow demand. It allows organisations to run their own execution infrastructure while creating and removing runner instances as jobs arrive and finish. This is particularly useful for enterprises that need control over build environments, network access, compute resources, or workload isolation without maintaining a permanently provisioned pool of runners.
One of the main themes in version 0.15.0 is reducing the work the controller performs to keep runner resources in sync. Runner status aggregation has also moved to metrics for EphemeralRunnerSet and AutoscalingRunnerSet, reducing the number of status updates sent to the Kubernetes API.

Welp, time to bring out that xkcd comic out again.
Modern computing systems and devices typically require pieces of crucial open-source software, typically maintained by unpaid or low-paid volunteers. Recently, a report collated a list of critical open-source projects, noting which of them are chronically underfunded and/or understaffed. The information is sobering: 11 out of 23 of the listed projects currently only have one or two maintainers, and funding is generally scarce and sometimes nonexistent.
The Data Drop's report on open-source maintainers identifies that having only one or two sets of eyes on critical pieces of software means that sooner or later something breaks — and it tends to do so in spectacular fashion, given its ubiquity. So, what happens when these projects, which are widely used across software, go underfunded or understaffed?

articles.title: AI is everywhere in Zoom product blitz - SiliconANGLE
articles.summary:
AI is everywhere in Zoom product blitz
Zoom Communications Inc. is expanding beyond videoconferencing with a shared intelligence layer designed to help artificial intelligence agents turn meetings, calls and customer interactions into completed work across business applications.
Announced at the Zoomtopia virtual conference, the Unified Context Layer anchors updates spanning workplace collaboration, customer service, developer tools, security, events and sales. The company’s strategy aims to address a persistent problem with enterprise AI: Assistants can capture conversations but often lack the history, permissions and connections needed to act on them.
Zoom combines conversation intelligence with documents and information from connected systems such as Salesforce Inc.’s customer relationship management, ServiceNow Inc.’s workflow management platform and Workday Inc.’s human capital management application. It builds a graph linking people, topics and decisions and updates those relationships in near real time, so agents don’t have to reconstruct context for each request.
“The context layer has already synthesized and distilled that information,” Chief Product Officer Russell Dicker said during a briefing. India-New Zealand trade pact kicks in
The agreement provides duty-free access to a range of Indian goods, including products from labour-intensive sectors such as textiles and leather.
The India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement (FTA), signed on April 27, came into effect on Tuesday, providing duty-free access to a range of Indian goods, including products from labour-intensive sectors such as textiles and leather.
It is the seventh trade pact to come into force in the last five years. The others are agreements with the UAE, Mauritius, the European Free Trade Association (EFTA) bloc, the UK, Oman and Australia.
Signed on April 27, 2026, the agreement follows negotiations launched in 2010, stalled in 2015 and revived in March 2025. The pact becomes India's 17th operational FTA.
According to experts, the sectors benefiting from the FTA are textiles and apparel, leather and footwear, engineering goods and auto components, gems and jewellery, agriculture and processed foods, pharmaceuticals, and other manufacturing industries.
Gulzar Didwania, Partner, Deloitte India, said the deal is expected to support higher FDI inflows into India, but the scale of any increase remains uncertain and will depend on private-sector investment decisions.
New Zealand has committed FDI worth USD 20 billion in over 15 years.

articles.title: GM to close Detroit battery-assembly plant, but not for reasons you might think | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
GM is closing a battery-assembly plant south of Detroit, a spokesperson confirmed to TechCrunch.
The Brownstown Battery Assembly Plant assembled battery packs for Cadillac’s flagship EV, the Celestiq, and both electric drive units (the motors that power the car) and battery packs for the Chevrolet Corvette E-Ray, a plug-in hybrid version of its famous sports car. Automotive News first reported the closure.
The closure is not related to GM’s electric vehicle strategy, the spokesperson said. Instead, GM leased the site, and the lease was nearing its end.
The employees and work at Brownstown will be moved to other GM facilities, though the company would not confirm which ones.
Like many automakers, GM’s electrification strategy was thrown a curveball after the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, the sweeping federal law signed last year, repealed incentives to produce and sell EVs.
Since then, the company has pared back its public comments on EVs, though it hasn’t given up on full electrification.
GM continues to produce a range of EVs, including the Chevrolet Silverado EV and the limited-time-only Chevrolet Bolt. It also continues researching new battery chemistries, including lithium-manganese-rich and sodium-ion, and it’s rolling out a new $900 million facility to speed commercialization.

Respan released an open-source AI gateway written in Rust on Tuesday, after spending two years building more than 100,000 lines of wrapper code around LiteLLM.
The new gateway replaces that system with a small core and plugins that handle model providers, routing, MCP tools, realtime voice, and security controls.
A LiteLLM upgrade breaks
The breaking point came in January 2026, when a routine LiteLLM upgrade caused intermittent connection failures. Respan rolled back the update but never figured out the problem.
“We still haven’t figured out the cause,” the company said in its Hacker News launch post.
Since then, its engineers have stopped upgrading LiteLLM directly, instead pulling in upstream fixes one at a time.
A small plugin core
To avoid another maintenance headache, the company borrowed an idea from Nginx, keeping the gateway’s core small and moving features like routing, model providers, and security into plugins. Developers can build their own using the same interfaces, without having to change the underlying code.

articles.title: TornadoVM 7 Enables GPU-Native Workloads From Java Applications

TornadoVM, an open-source heterogeneous GPU programming framework for Java has reached version 7.3, a major milestone for the project.
InfoQ previously covered the project in December 2025 and in 2022.
TornadoVM automatically accelerates Java programs on multi-core CPUs and GPUs. Rather than replacing existing JVMs, it works alongside them and provides a rich GPU programming ecosystem in Java that you can use with any mainstream JDK distribution such as OpenJDK, Graalvm, Temurin, or Zulu.
It offloads Java code to hardware backends, manages memory between the Java heap and accelerators, and runs the resulting compute kernels. This makes it a useful building block for modern cloud and machine learning workloads.
During development, TornadoVM compiles the source Java code to OpenCL and Apple Metal backends. The idea is that you can develop locally on your laptop and use the hardware available locally, and then deploy into a server that has Nvidia GPUs, and achieve major performance improvements - a form of "Write Once, Run Anywhere" for modern ML workloads.
Version 7 brings several architectural changes. The backends now use the Foreign Function & Memory (FFM) API in place of the Java Native Interface (JNI). The experimental JVM Compiler Interface (JVMCI) dependency has also been removed. According to the team, TornadoVM now sources "all compiler metadata through a reflection + ASM + Unsafe layer" which is the single, uniform path on every supported JDK (21, 25, 26 and 27).

articles.title: Mozilla, Google, Apple block compromised eMudhra CA certificates
articles.summary:
Certificate authority eMudhra revoked eight compromised intermediate certificates after researchers found their private keys were so weak that anyone could recover them almost instantly and use them to forge trusted certificates for legitimate websites.
Major browsers and operating systems trusted the compromised certificates, potentially allowing attackers to impersonate legitimate websites and intercept encrypted communications.
A security researcher known as Wayne discovered the weakness on October 17 while scanning publicly available certificate data.
According to Mozilla's incident report, all eight certificates used P-384 private keys generated in April 2025 that had values smaller than 256, allowing anyone to recover them by testing just 256 possible numbers.
To demonstrate the weakness, security researcher Flüpke published one of the compromised private keys on GitHub, showing that the private key for eMudhra's "EM OV TLS CA - G3C" certificate had a value of just 4.
BleepingComputer independently verified that the published key matches one of the revoked certificates.
In a response to Mozilla, eMudhra blamed the issue on an error in a script used to generate the certificates in April 2025. The company said the error generated a second set of weaker keys that were mistakenly selected for certificate signing because they had labels similar to the properly generated keys.
Some of the resulting certificates were also submitted to Sectigo for cross-signing.

articles.title: Meta drops the word "train" from its commercial TOS after AI backlash
articles.summary:
Hoping to quell criticism, Meta has dropped the word “train” from its “streamlined” commercial terms of service that kick in on October 30.
Last week, Meta faced backlash after legal experts warned that the tech giant’s sweeping new commercial terms of service seemed to give Meta permission to endlessly scrape websites linked on business pages. Talking to Nieman Lab, experts suggested that Meta could possibly use the policy to avoid millions in licensing fees from news organizations by requiring all business users to share a wealth of AI training data simply for running a business page.
A Meta spokesperson confirmed that Meta did not alert users to the changed language following backlash. This potentially only adds to confusion ahead of the policy rollout. In response to backlash, Meta’s spokesperson provided a statement to Ars, acknowledging Nieman Lab’s initial report but not its follow-up report reiterating experts’ concerns:
“We’ve heard you and want to clarify: the crawling terms we consolidated only applied to our ads and business products, and we’ve clarified that in the terms themselves. It does not change how Meta uses web crawlers. As always, content owners can use robots.txt to signal their preferences. This is not about scraping news sites, and these updates don’t give us new rights that supersede those preferences.”
The same experts who sounded the initial alarms were not impressed by Meta’s updates, which they told Nieman Lab do not go far enough to protect busi…

articles.title: A judge lets Denuvo subpoena Discord, Reddit, and Steam to unmask the cracker Voices38
articles.summary:
Connecting the dots: Denuvo has spent the past few weeks trying to uncover Voices38's true identity. The mysterious cracker has been wreaking havoc on the company's notorious DRM and anti-tamper technology, and Denuvo is now turning to lawyers in a bid to unmask the skilled coder.
Denuvo's first attempt to uncover Voices38's real identity was unsuccessful because the company tried to obtain too much data at once. Now, a California federal judge has granted the Irdeto-owned DRM maker's revised subpoena requests. Several internet companies will soon have to respond to Denuvo's lawyers, but Voices38 could still remain a John Doe in the end.
Denuvo's latest legal assault began earlier this month, when the company asked a judge to help identify the unnamed cracker operating under the "Voices38" moniker. The request was part of Denuvo's lawsuit against Voices38, which centers on the cracker's alleged violations of the DMCA's anti-circumvention provisions.
Denuvo initially asked the judge to approve 46 separate subpoena requests targeting Discord, Valve, Reddit, and other internet companies. The subpoenas sought potential names and email addresses, along with additional data related to payments and financial transactions, login logs, comment histories, and more.
According to Judge Haywood S. Gilliam Jr., Denuvo's requests went too far. Although the company was seeking to uncover Voices38's identity, the subpoenas extended well beyond the information needed to identify the individual…

articles.title: Un agricultor halló en su campo de maíz en Minnesota los restos de un cohete chino de 3,35 metros
articles.summary:
Un agricultor del condado de Stevens, en Minnesota, encontró un objeto metálico circular de 3,35 metros de diámetro mientras cosechaba maíz el 14 de octubre. El análisis de Ars Technica concluyó que se trata de la etapa superior de un cohete chino Zhuque-2E.
La Oficina del Sheriff del condado de Stevens recibió el aviso ese mismo día y confirmó el hallazgo en Scott Township, una zona rural al oeste del estado. “Los agentes confirmaron que había un objeto metálico grande, de unos 3,35 metros de diámetro, presuntamente un objeto espacial”, informó la oficina en un comunicado.
Las autoridades trabajan junto a agencias estatales y federales para identificar al dueño del objeto y coordinar su retiro del campo, aunque no precisaron una fecha para completar esa tarea. Según informaron, el objeto no representó ningún peligro para la población mientras permaneció en el terreno.
Un cohete que recorrió medio planeta antes de caer
El 15 de septiembre, un cohete Zhuque-2E de la empresa china LandSpace despegó desde Dongfeng, una zona de lanzamientos comerciales ubicada junto al centro militar de Jiuquan, en el noroeste de China. Media hora después del despegue, liberó diez satélites en una órbita polar circular de unos 900 kilómetros de altitud.
Los satélites pertenecen a la red Qianfan, también llamada “Mil Velas”, el proyecto con el que China busca competir con Starlink, la constelación de SpaceX. Desde 2024, el país lanzó 258 satélites Qianfan, con el objetivo de llegar a 1.296 unidade…

articles.title: Console portable Xbox : pourquoi elle n'utilisera pas Windows — Frandroid
articles.summary:
Malgré des vagues de licenciement sans fin et des chiffres de vente décevants, Xbox tient toujours debout et ne compte pas se laisser devancer dans la course aux consoles de nouvelle génération. articles.summary:
Outre Revolut, d’autres banques britanniques comme Lloyds, HSBC ou NatWest enregistrent ce mardi une vague de signalements. Au même moment, Google Cloud reconnaît un incident d’ampleur sur ses serveurs de Londres, sans en préciser l’origine.
La panne de Revolut, qui bloque depuis ce mardi 20 octobre 2026 les cartes et application de nombreux clients jusqu'en France, pourrait bien n'être que la partie visible de l'immense iceberg qui cache les banques… britanniques. Après Revolut, plusieurs grandes banques britanniques en panne

articles.summary:
A threat actor breached TeamUpdraft's website, a developer of popular WordPress backup and security plugins, potentially compromising UpdraftCentral connection keys that can send commands to connected websites.
TeamUpdraft detected unauthorized access to its infrastructure over the weekend and believes that the hacker accessed the customer database.
The developer offers several WordPress tools for backup, storage, and site management:

- UpdraftCentral: for managing multiple sites remotely
- UpdraftVault: for cloud backup storage
- UpdraftClone: for creating staging websites

The vendor says it believes the threat actor accessed its customer database, which included details about the customer and billing, order history, as well as more sensitive information:
- password hashes
- two-factor authentication settings
- connection keys for UpdraftCentral, UpdraftVault, and UpdraftClone services

articles.title: Spotify : cette nouvelle vérification va faire une hécatombe sur les partages de compte
articles.summary:
Le partage de compte et les règles des plateformes de streaming : une histoire qui semble ne jamais finir. Justement, Spotify a décidé de sévir concernant son abonnement Premium Famille, qui permet de partager un compte Premium avec les membres de sa famille qui « vivent sous le même toit ». La plateforme de streaming musical semble estimer que trop de personnes partagent un compte Famille Premium, sans vivre sous le même toit. Elle a donc décidé de mettre en place un nouveau système de vérification.
Un QR code dynamique à scanner
Spotify a décidé de s’attaquer aux personnes qui partagent un abonnement Premium Famille, sans vivre sous le même toit. Comme le rapporte Android Authority, des utilisateurs de Reddit signalent une demande de vérification de la part de la plateforme de streaming musical. Pour être plus précis, ceux qui bénéficient d’un abonnement Premium Famille doivent scanner un QR code avec le propriétaire du compte Premium.
Point important : il s’agit d’un QR code dynamique, autrement dit, il est renouvelé toutes les quelques secondes, ce qui complique sensiblement la réalisation d’une capture d’écran pour ensuite le scanner. De ce fait, ce système de vérification par scan de QR code dynamique permet de vérifier que les deux personnes se situent à proximité l’une de l’autre, et donc vivent bel et bien sous le même toit.

articles.title: Sicherheitslücke in Routern entdeckt: Wie ein 16 Jahre alter Fehler erneut zum Problem wird
articles.summary:
Sicherheitslücke in Routern entdeckt: Wie ein 16 Jahre alter Fehler erneut zum Problem wird
Router vernetzen zahlreiche Haushalte mit dem Internet. Sie können aber schnell zum Einfallstor für Cyberkriminelle werden, wenn du nicht die richtigen Einstellungen am Router vornimmst. Gleiches gilt, wenn es eine Lücke im System der Router gibt, die lange Zeit unerkannt bleibt. So soll es laut einem Sicherheitsforscher schon seit 2010 der Fall sein. Laut ihm sind von der Lücke potenziell Millionen Geräte betroffen.
Neue Router-Sicherheitslücke: Welche Gefahr droht
Die Warnung stammt vom belgischen Sicherheitsforscher Quentin Kaiser, der die Sicherheitslücke „WPSplinter“ getauft hat. Im Grunde handelt es sich dabei um zwei Fehler, die in der Software von Broadcom zu finden sind. Broadcoms Wi-Fi-Implementierung wird laut Kaiser von dutzenden Routerherstellern genutzt. Dadurch finden sich die Fehler in hunderten Produkten und potenziell in „Millionen von Broadcom-basierten Access-Points weltweit“.
Die Fehler sorgen dafür, dass sich Unbefugte über WPS (Wi-Fi Protected Setup) Zugriff auf die Router verschaffen können. Über das Feature können Endgeräte und Router ohne Passworteingabe miteinander verknüpft werden, indem eine WPS-Taste auf dem Router gedrückt wird, während das Endgerät ebenfalls einen WPS-Prozess startet. Laut Kaiser kann eine manipulierte WPS-Nachricht eingeschleust werden, um den Speicher der Router zu verändern.

Over email, the pair unpacked common misconceptions surrounding esports, their collaboration to expand PUBG Mobile esports around the world and where they hope to see the game go in the years to come.
What are common misconceptions that you hear about esports?
Alban Dechelotte: One misconception is that esports is a digital version of traditional sport. It is its own form of
competition, with its own culture, audiences and ways of building fandom. When traditional sports organizations treat it only as a simulation of what they already do, they can miss the opportunity to reach completely different communities.

articles.title: How to choose customer support software for your business
articles.summary:
How to choose customer support software for your business
The key considerations for choosing customer support software
Customer support is essential to building a successful business, and software plays a central role in your support operations. Customer support software makes it easy to track customers’ inquiries and respond to them promptly.
Some support requests can be complicated and require many back-and-forth interactions to resolve. Support software ensures your team keeps up with these requests and solves customers’ issues, no matter how tough.
Given its crucial role in your business, customer support software isn’t something to choose lightly. You need to carefully consider the best software, depending on your business type, size, and the complexity of the support requests you handle.
This guide explains what customer support software is, how it works, the key features to look out for, and the core considerations for selecting the best software.
What is customer support software?
Customer support software is the digital tool your business uses to receive, organize, and respond to customer requests.
Think of it as a mail sorting system for your customer inquiries. When a customer sends a request, it’ll be immediately logged into your support system and categorized based on the details. Then, it can be assigned to a specific team or team member based on predefined settings.

articles.title: OpenAI acquires startup Orchestra Bio to beef up its biotech business | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
OpenAI on Tuesday acquired a four-year-old AI biotech software startup called Orchestra Bio, the company announced on its website. Terms of the deal were not disclosed, but the startup had reportedly raised around $20 million as of 2025 from backers like Andreessen Horowitz, Atria, and 8VC.
Orchestra creates AI agents that help biotech companies manage the minutiae of drug-discovery operations, from tracking finances to resolving scheduling issues with clinical trials.
OpenAI says it’s adding Orchestra’s team and technology to work on Rosalind, its AI model for life sciences research, and to its related Rosalind Workbench tool, a harness that aims to help researchers plan experiments and analyze results. OpenAI has already won some big names as customers for Rosalind, including, it says, Moderna and Novo Nordisk.
The acquisition is a classic example of how the biggest AI labs (namely OpenAI and Anthropic) are building ever more software for the biggest industries, like pharma. In the startup world, there is an ongoing fear that at any moment, the labs will launch new features and become competitors. In this case, Orchestra is getting absorbed, rather than stomped out.

articles.title: AI operating model: Dell treats company knowledge as its edge - SiliconANGLE
articles.summary:
Dell sees company knowledge, not AI models, as its competitive edge
As AI agents take on more work that people used to do, enterprises need an AI operating model to match. That means changing how people, processes and work are organized, not just which tools get deployed.
Dell Technologies Inc. has spent close to two years running fully autonomous agents inside its own business, and those lessons now shape its advice to customers. Companies that adopt agents without changing how they are organized accomplish very little, according to John Roese (pictured), global chief technology officer and chief AI officer of Dell.
“If you adopt AI technology but are unwilling or unable to change your operating model, you’re going to run your business just like you did before AI, but you’re going to do AI to it,” Roese said. “You’re going to have a bad experience because … if you apply agents to your company, what you are doing is redistributing work between people and machines.”
Roese spoke with theCUBE Research’s Dave Vellante at the Dell Technologies New York Symposium, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed why AI agents force companies to rethink their operating models and how enterprises can protect the knowledge that sets them apart. (* Disclosure below.)
Why the AI operating model starts with knowledge

articles.title: JustWatch, which tackles streaming fragmentation, launches own streaming service
articles.summary:
Since launching in 2015, JustWatch has helped people navigate the growing number of streaming services by providing a guide on where to find movies they want to stream. Now JustWatch has its own streaming service and wants people to subscribe.
Launched today, JustWatch TV offers some movies available for free with ads that aren’t free on any other streaming service, including Green Room (2015), Locke (2013), and Sing Sing (2023). Other free movies include Fiddlin’ (2018), Friday the 13th (1980), and Hotel Mumbai (2018). I could play movies available for free on JustWatch TV without creating an account.
JustWatch TV also has movies you can rent.
The streaming service also sells a subscription for people who don’t want to watch JustWatch’s library with ads. It’s currently $4 per month or $50 for a lifetime subscription. The latter is only available for a “limited” time, a company spokesperson told Ars Technica. The rep was unable to confirm how long JustWatch will sell the lifetime subscription.
Upon my perusal, JustWatch TV’s library seems limited and somewhat dated. That’s not necessarily a bad idea. Howdy, a Roku-owned streaming service with a similarly lackluster library compared to other services that costs $3/month without ads, reportedly had 1 million subscribers six months into launch.

articles.title: Microsoft's Bing Wallpaper App Hijacks Desktop Clicks to Promote Bing.com
articles.summary:
Tuesday, October 20th 2026
Microsoft's Bing Wallpaper App Hijacks Desktop Clicks to Promote Bing.com
Microsoft's popular wallpaper application, Bing Wallpaper, has now been transformed into adware, according to a new report by Windows Latest. When a user clicks on an empty area of the desktop—not on any icon or menu—the application redirects them to Bing.com, Microsoft's search engine. Normally, this behavior would not be acceptable and would likely trigger a strong reaction from the community. However, Microsoft has limited this issue to occur only once every 24 hours. Repeated clicks after the initial activation do not open another browser window. Testing has confirmed that this behavior persists after the waiting period, even when Google Chrome is set as the default browser.
Interestingly, Microsoft tested a similar feature in 2025, which included a clearly labeled setting in Bing Wallpaper that allowed a desktop click to open Bing. At that time, the feature could be turned off, but this option is not available in the latest version of the application. Microsoft has removed the ability to disable this feature, meaning that every 24 hours, a desktop click will redirect to Bing.com. This change leaves users with less control over an action that is unrelated to managing wallpaper. The application has also reportedly displayed prompts encouraging users to make Bing their default search engine across installed browsers, even when the default browser is Google Chrome or another …

articles.title: WhatsApp s'attaque à Safari avec un navigateur intégré sur iOS

La fonction existe depuis l’an dernier pour certains liens d’entreprises ; elle s’étendrait désormais à l’ensemble des conversations. De quoi éviter le détour par Safari ou le navigateur par défaut de votre iPhone.
Tous les liens, sans quitter la discussion
Le chantier se cache dans la bêta 26.41.10.72, distribuée via TestFlight. Un réglage dédié apparaît dans les paramètres des discussions, pour activer ou couper le navigateur intégré à tout moment. Durante los últimos años, el término "ultraprocesado" se ha convertido en el gran villano de la nutrición moderna. El sistema NOVA, que clasifica los alimentos según su grado de procesamiento industrial, ha calado hondo tanto en las políticas de la salud pública como en la percepción general. Sin embargo, la evidencia científica más reciente está empezando a dibujar una escala de grises en la que ni todo es malo ni todo es bueno por el mero hecho de salir de una fábrica.
Un análisis reciente que nos llega desde Italia, publicado en la revista Foods, ilustra perfectamente este problema de categorización. Tras analizar más de 13.000 productos del mercado italiano, los investigadores confirmaron que casi dos tercios de los ultraprocesados sacaban un suspenso en el Nutri-Score con una D o una E, siendo los snacks los peor parados.
Pero descubrieron una enorme variabilidad interna, puesto que el nivel de procesamiento por sí solo no basta para predecir el impacto de un alimento. Aquí la densidad energética, la hiperpalatabilidad y el perfil de nutrientes juegan un papel diferencial que la clasificación generalista tiende a enmascarar.
Es importante. Esta heterogeneidad tiene un impacto clínico directo, puesto que en los últimos años grandes cohortes epidemiológicas han demostrado que en todos los subgrupos de ultraprocesados se comportan igual en nuestro organismo. articles.title: Chris Lattner: AI Code Generation Doesn't Solve Software Engineering - EE Times
articles.summary:
For AI chip companies, the promise of AI-based coding agents is compelling: generate the low-level kernels needed to get a model running on new hardware, optimize them for performance, and do it without the software engineering resources traditionally required.
But according to Chris Lattner, CEO of AI software startup Modular (recently acquired by Qualcomm, where he now serves as executive VP of software engineering), chip companies should be wary of the limits of AI code generation. Making a kernel run fast is a very different problem from building software infrastructure we can depend on, he told EE Times in an exclusive interview.
“Agents are good, but they’re like anything else; it’s a tool, and you have to use it the right way,” Lattner said. “What I’ve seen with agents is they make tons of throwaway code. So, if you’re building a product, you don’t want to agent-generate everything.”
Agentic code generation makes sense for projects that are well-defined and limited in scope (e.g., “make this kernel go fast”), which can be quantified, measured, and validated, Lattner said, but bigger projects require product design and software engineering and can’t be delegated to agents.
“If you’re a startup and you only care about getting one model working, or getting it to go fast, [then go ahead,] use AI tools to prove it’s possible,” he said. “But that’s not going to be great for when you want to sell your chip to someone else, and they want to run a model you don’t have access to…

articles.title: Millions of routers can be hijacked over Wi-Fi thanks to a 16-year-old bug
articles.summary:
Why it matters: Chipmakers ship buggy code all the time, that alone isn't news. What makes WPSplinter stand out is that Broadcom apparently did issue a fix eight years ago, but that fix never reached the routers sitting in people's homes. Furthermore, the lack of a CVE kept the problem invisible to the advisories and patch pipelines that router makers and ISPs rely on.
Security researcher Quentin Kaiser detailed the flaw at the Hexacon conference in Paris on October 16. He calls it WPSplinter, a name he only gave it because Broadcom refused to issue an official identifier.
The bug sits in Broadcom's old code for WPS, the feature that lets you connect a device by pressing a button on the router instead of typing a password. That code mishandles how certain messages are exchanged and with the right sequence of them, it lets an attacker read the router's memory or run external code on the device.
The attacker doesn't need the Wi-Fi password or a completed WPS pairing. Being within radio range is enough. This also isn't the WPS PIN weakness that made headlines in the early 2010s. The problem is Broadcom's code, not WPS itself.
Kaiser's demos make the risk concrete. On an Askey TCG3000 gateway supplied by Orange Belgium, his exploit pulled the Wi-Fi key out of the device's NVRAM, sent it back over the air, and then used it to join the network. On a different device, a Proximus BBOX3V+ made by Sagemcom, he got a remote shell running entirely over Wi-Fi, with no internet connection …

The gross merchandise value of India’s ecommerce market expanded roughly 25% on a year-on-year basis to about $38 billion in the first half of 2026, marking its strongest H1 performance in four years.
India's online retail market is projected to cross $90 billion in 2026, registering an annual growth of 22-24%, its fastest expansion in five years, driven by everyday consumption categories such as grocery rather than mobile phones, Redseer Strategy Consultants said in a report.
According to the analysis, ecommerce gross merchandise value (GMV) expanded roughly 25% year-on-year to about $38 billion in the first half (H1) of 2026, marking its strongest H1 performance in four years.
While online retail accelerated, mobile sales remained flat at 0% growth during the first half and are projected to grow by just 2-3% across the full year due to sharp price increases curbing sales volumes.
Consequently, the grocery segment is poised to overtake mobile phones as the second-largest category in Indian ecommerce, behind fashion.
"This year, India's online retail is growing fastest where demand is steadiest," said Kushal Bhatnagar, Partner at Redseer.
The report noted that grocery, beauty and personal care (BPC), and home and furniture will account for about 40% of overall online retail GMV in 2026 and roughly three-fifths of the incremental GMV added during the year.

articles.title: Cops raid office of RFK Jr. allies planning “unethical” vaccine trial on babies
articles.summary:
Police in Guinea-Bissau raided the offices of Danish researchers on Monday, seizing doses of hepatitis B vaccine intended for a vaccine trial for newborns. International health experts have called the trial “unethical,” but anti-vaccine Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has attempted to fund it with US taxpayer dollars.
Under Kennedy, the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention announced in December that it had awarded the Danish researchers—led by married couple Peter Aaby and Christine Stabell Benn of Bandim Health Project—an unsolicited $1.6 million grant to run the trial. Aaby and Stabell Benn are controversial vaccine researchers who claim vaccines cause overlooked harms. They have been repeatedly praised by Kennedy, but are currently under investigation for alleged scientific misconduct by Danish authorities.
Plans for the trial were halted in January as widespread condemnation erupted over the trial’s design, which would potentially expose thousands of newborns in the country to hepatitis B, risking a lifelong infection that can lead to liver cirrhosis, cancer, and premature death. Outrage flared again after a Rolling Stone story earlier this month claimed the CDC set aside another $1.6 million in funding in late September and planned to move forward with the trial.

The Canadian company’s devices must be light enough for a fish to carry without materially changing its behavior, yet contain the electronics and battery needed to transmit useful data from underwater. The result is a design problem in which mass, power consumption, and reliability constrain one another.
The Bedford, Nova Scotia-based company develops acoustic telemetry equipment for researchers studying fish movement and behavior. Miniature transmitters travel with the animals; receivers detect their signals.

Obwohl Windows 11 ein modernes Betriebssystem ist und Microsoft darauf bedacht ist, viele Neuerungen zu implementieren, gibt es darin noch Relikte fast vergessener Zeiten. Dazu zählt etwa ein Feature, das nur wegen eines Kultspiels in Windows eingefügt wurde. Daneben gibt es aber auch alte Regeln, die Windows-User:innen heute noch einen Strich durch die Rechnung, oder besser gesagt die Dateibenennung, machen können.
Warum Windows 11 manche Dateinamen verbietet
Wie Windows Latest berichtet, gibt es eine Reihe von Namen und Kürzeln, die nicht für Dateien in Windows 11 genutzt werden dürfen. Versuchen es User:innen doch, verweigert das Betriebssystem die Eingabe und drängt darauf, einen anderen Namen für die Datei oder den Ordner zu wählen. Insgesamt sind es sechs Namenskategorien, teilweise mit mehreren Vertretern ihrer Art.
So können Dateien unter Windows 11 weder „CON“, „PRN“, „AUX“, noch „NUL“ genannt werden. Auch bei „COM1“ bis zu „COM9“ sowie „LPT1 bis zu „LPT9“ sperrt sich das Betriebssystem. Wie Microsoft-Entwickler Raymond Chen in einem Blog-Post schon vor einigen Jahren erklärte, stammt diese Regelung noch aus alten DOS-Zeiten. Denn damals waren die Begriffe für verschiedene Geräte reserviert – „CON“ für die Konsole, „PRN“ für den Drucker und „COM1“ bis „COM9“ für die physischen Anschlüsse des Systems. „NUL“ hingegen löschte die Dateien sofort wieder. „AUX“ steht für sekundäre Geräte und „LPT“ fü…

“All PHP users are encouraged to prepare now so they can upgrade as soon as the release is available,” the advisory stated. “We reserve the right to release earlier should details of either vulnerability become public, or should evidence of active exploitation appear in the wild.”

The report showed a video of an exploit tool dubbed PHP2Shell executing code on webservers running WordPress 7.1.3, MediaWiki 1.46.2, phpBB 3.3.17, Magento 2.4.9, Joomla 6.2.0, Laravel 13.36.0, Laravel 8.83.29, Symphony 8.1.9, Drupal 11.4.10, and WHMCS 9.0.9, all of which use PHP. A video depicting the tool has been reposted here.
Attempts to locate the unconfirmed report were unsuccessful, but security firm watchTowr said it claimed to affect every PHP version from PHP 5, released in 2004, onward. The security firm went on to say it has confirmed that the vulnerabilities, tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, are real.

La función, llamada Locked Chats, mueve cada conversación protegida a una sección separada del historial regular, de los chats fijados y de los resultados de búsqueda dentro de la aplicación. Según la empresa, está pensada para quien habla de temas personales o planea una sorpresa y no quiere exponer esa charla al mostrarle otra cosa a un familiar o amigo.
A diferencia de los Chats Temporales, que generan una sesión aparte que desaparece y no queda guardada en el historial, los chats bloqueados se conservan y pueden volver a abrirse en cualquier momento con la misma autenticación.
OpenAI aclaró que bloquear un chat no equivale a cifrarlo de punta a punta ni crea una bóveda encriptada aparte. Tampoco cambia cuánto tiempo la empresa conserva esa conversación, ni borra la información que ChatGPT ya había incorporado a su memoria antes de activar el bloqueo.
La compañía explicó además que la opción no modifica la configuración de “mejorar el modelo para todos”, con la que algunos usuarios autorizan que sus conversaciones se usen para entrenar el sistema.

Inception says Mercury 3 beats GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5 at up to 8x the speed
Diffusion language model startup Inception AI Inc. today released Mercury 3, its new flagship model.
In the company’s own benchmarks, Mercury 3 beat OpenAI Group PBC’s GPT-6 Luna and Anthropic PBC’s Claude Haiku 5.5 on eight of 12 tests at four to eight times their speed.
The release takes on the main doubt about Inception’s approach. Co-founder and Chief Executive Stefano Ermon said the question the company has heard most since Mercury 1 “is whether diffusion can scale.” As he sees it, the limits come down to “compute and data, not fundamental algorithmic barriers.”
GPT-6 Luna and Haiku 5.5 write their answers the conventional way, one token after another. A Mercury model drafts the whole response up front, then refines every position in parallel over a few passes. Inception clocked Mercury 3 at 1,068 tokens per second on Nvidia Corp. graphics processing units, with Haiku 5.5 reaching about 240 in the same comparison and GPT-6 Luna about 130.
Inception has not disclosed a parameter count for Mercury 3, saying only that it is more than 40 times the size of Mercury 1. The context window grows to 1 million tokens, up from the 260,000 that Mercury 2.5 handled. Ermon said training on Mercury 3’s successor is already under way.

Rumor: NVIDIA RTX 6060 May Be Years Away, and Possibly Slower Than the PS6
Anyone holding out for an affordable next-gen NVIDIA card might have a long wait. Hardware leaker Kepler_L2 claims on NeoGAF that the GeForce RTX 6060 will "launch much later," adding that, based on recent trends, he doubts it will even match the PlayStation 6. He was replying to a forum member who argued the PS6 would compete with the RTX 6060, in the same thread where he claimed the console's RAM and storage alone cost over $680. Kepler didn't give an actual date, and the 2029 figure going around seems to be an extrapolation. Both Kepler and kopite7kimi have placed NVIDIA's Rubin-based RTX 60 series in 2028, and the x60 cards usually trail the flagship by a few months. The RTX 5060 arrived under four months after the RTX 5090, while the RTX 4060 took over eight months to follow the RTX 4090. 
With a flagship launch around mid-2028 or later, that could push the RTX 6060 into 2029. That said, the "much later" comment seems to be relative to the PS6, which is reportedly targeting late 2027, so the exact timing is still anyone's guess. Kepler didn't say why, but the ongoing memory shortage looks like the obvious suspect. NVIDIA reportedly postponed its RTX 50 SUPER refresh earlier this year to prioritize AI products that use the same GDDR7 memory, and the company recently admitted that RTX 5090 supply is tight. Esa lógica no ha desaparecido, pero empieza a moverse más deprisa. La inteligencia artificial ya no solo ayuda a escribir código o buscar información: algunos sistemas pueden recibir un objetivo, trabajar durante horas y encadenar por sí mismos buena parte de las tareas que antes mantenían ocupado a un atacante.

Cyberpunk 2077 Gets a Surprise Update This Week, Tied to Edgerunners 2
CD Projekt RED has announced Cyberpunk 2077 Update 2.5, a free patch arriving on October 22 for PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X|S. The Switch 2 version will follow "shortly," though there's no date for it yet. The update ties into Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2, which premiered all ten episodes on Netflix on October 20, and brings new items and features inspired by the anime. So far, CDPR has only teased cyberware customization and a new dual-wielding playstyle. This one is quite a surprise, since Cyberpunk 2077 hasn't received an update in over a year. Update 2.3 arrived in July 2025 with FSR 4, XeSS frame generation, and VRR for consoles, and it looked like the game's final major update at the time. A smaller 2.31 patch followed in September 2025, and the studio has since put most of its focus on The Witcher 4, which has a 2028 release window. Interestingly, 2.31 launched on Switch 2 alongside the other platforms, so the staggered release this time is a bit unusual. CDPR hasn't said anything about PC-specific changes like new upscalers or ray tracing tweaks, so it's reasonable to wait for the patch notes on October 21 before expecting anything on that front.

People still make the final call.
Scientists should be able to use the combined tools to make discoveries and “manage the work needed to turn them into treatments,” OpenAI said. Terms were not disclosed, and OpenAI gave no timeline for when Orchestra’s agents will show up in its products.

Ganz anders sieht es beim Streaming aus: Die Werbeerlöse im Videostreaming sollen um 15 Prozent auf rund 2,5 Milliarden Euro steigen. Auch die Einnahmen aus Audiostreaming-Werbung wachsen der Prognose zufolge um zehn Prozent auf 147 Millionen Euro.

articles.title: L’Europe part aussi à la conquête de la Lune : voici OASIS, la future “station-service” de l’ESA sur notre satellite

L’Agence spatiale européenne (ESA) ne compte pas regarder passer la course à la Lune. Elle prépare sa propre infrastructure, pensée avec des briques européennes de bout en bout.
Alors que la Chine et les États-Unis se tirent la bourre pour implanter la toute première base lunaire permanente, le rôle que jouera l’Europe dans cette conquête est plus que jamais remis en question. Jared Isaacman, patron de la NASA, a été clair : personne n’est garanti d’être partenaire, même s’il s’agit d’alliés de longue date. Dans ce contexte, l’ESA dégaine sa propre carte.
À quoi va servir OASIS, exactement ?
L’agence spatiale vient en effet de présenter OASIS, pour « Outpost for Advanced Scientific Investigation Station », une « station-service » lunaire. Son rôle : fournir l’énergie, les communications et le stockage de données dont les instruments ont besoin pour travailler sur le sol lunaire pendant de très longues périodes, et cela inclut la nuit.
Or, privée de Soleil et soumise à un froid extrême, l’électronique peut y être gravement endommagée. OASIS doit donc capter l’énergie solaire le jour et la stocker dans une batterie. « Il permettra aux charges utiles de fonctionner pendant des années à la surface de la Lune, en activité pendant les jours lunaires et en mode veille pendant les nuits lunaires », étaye l'agence.

articles.title: Google Chrome vai exibir novo alerta para sites suspeitos • Tecnoblog
articles.summary:
Google Chrome vai exibir novo alerta para sites suspeitos
Navegador usa Gemini para identificar possíveis golpes e adiciona proteção contra comandos maliciosos.
O Google anunciou nesta terça-feira (20/10) uma nova camada de alerta no Chrome para páginas suspeitas. Em vez de exibir a tradicional tela vermelha usada para sites classificados como perigosos, o navegador poderá mostrar primeiro um pop-up com o aviso de que aquela página “não parece certa”.
A mudança estará disponível para usuários do modo de Proteção Avançada do Safe Browsing. Segundo o Google, o Chrome também usará modelos do Gemini executados na nuvem para analisar possíveis golpes oe ganhou uma proteção específica contra ataques do tipo ClickFix.

articles.title: Mozilla y Google bloquearon ocho certificados digitales que podían falsificar cualquier sitio web
articles.summary:
Mozilla y Google bloquearon ocho certificados digitales de la empresa india eMudhra después de que un investigador anónimo, identificado solo como Wayne, demostró que podía falsificar la identidad de cualquier sitio de internet.
Los certificados digitales son las credenciales que permiten a un navegador confirmar que una página es quien dice ser y cifrar el tráfico mediante el protocolo HTTPS. Quien controla la clave privada de uno de esos certificados puede hacerse pasar por cualquier sitio web.
Seis de los ocho certificados comprometidos se usan para asegurar conexiones web y los otros dos para firmar programas de software. Todos están respaldados por los programas de confianza de Mozilla, Microsoft, Apple y Google, de los que dependen la mayoría de los navegadores y sistemas operativos del mundo.
El problema no estuvo en el cifrado sino en cómo eMudhra generó las claves. Una clave de ese tipo debería tener alrededor de 384 bits de aleatoriedad, miles de billones de combinaciones posibles. Las ocho claves filtradas tenían apenas entre tres y ocho bits, lo que las hacía recuperables en segundos.
Un ingeniero de Mozilla recuperó las ocho claves por su cuenta en menos de dos horas, sin conocer el método del primer reportante, y confirmó así que la falla era real. Otros investigadores le pidieron a asistentes de inteligencia artificial que resolvieran el problema como si fuera un desafío de seguridad informática, y lo lograron en el primer intento.

articles.title: Investigadores hallaron más de 6.800 chats privados de la IA Muse de Meta expuestos en internet
articles.summary:
Claroc, una firma de ciberseguridad encontró más de 6.800 conversaciones que usuarios compartieron con Muse, el asistente de inteligencia artificial de Meta, accesibles para cualquiera en internet sin que nadie les hubiera enviado el enlace.
La empresa, especializada en ciberseguridad, llegó a esas conversaciones mediante una búsqueda de DNS pasivo, una técnica que registra los nombres de dominio que ya circularon en internet. Abrió solo algunos cientos de los enlaces hallados y dejó el resto sin revisar.
El problema nace del propio diseño de Muse. Cuando un usuario pide compartir una charla con el asistente, Meta genera una página pública y arma la dirección web con el título que el usuario le puso a esa conversación. Ese nombre queda registrado en los servidores de DNS, visibles para cualquiera que sepa buscarlos.
Eso significa que no hace falta recibir el enlace para entrar a la página: alcanza con rastrear los nombres de dominio del servicio, algo que Claroc hizo con una sola consulta a una base de datos comercial. El sitio urlscan.io, que cualquiera puede usar, ya guardaba más de 75 capturas de esas páginas.
Qué se encontró en los datos de Muse
Entre los enlaces revisados, Claroc halló un documento con los apuntes de una persona que se preparaba para una entrevista confidencial con un laboratorio de inteligencia artificial, con el nombre del contacto interno y el horario exacto de la reunión.

articles.summary:
Un canal de YouTube dedicado a la metalurgia y la ingeniería casera construyó un refrigerador que funciona con fuego, agua y sal de carretera, sin depender de un compresor eléctrico convencional. El proyecto, desarrollado por Greenhill Forge, logró enfriar una sección del dispositivo hasta los 5 °C (41 °F) mientras la temperatura ambiente rondaba los 16 °C (61 °F), un resultado que el propio canal documentó en video.
La propuesta retoma un principio de ingeniería centenario con una aplicación actual: la posibilidad de generar frío en lugares donde la electricidad es escasa o poco confiable.
El principio detrás del sistema: absorción refrigerante
El dispositivo se basa en la refrigeración por absorción, una técnica que existe desde hace más de un siglo y que prescinde del compresor eléctrico para hacer circular el refrigerante. En su lugar, utiliza calor para impulsar una reacción química que produce el efecto de enfriamiento.
El diseño de Greenhill Forge se compone de dos secciones principales: un generador y un absorbedor. El generador contiene una solución de cloruro de calcio y agua destilada. Cuando el fuego calienta esa mezcla, el vapor de agua se separa de la solución y viaja a través de una tubería hasta un condensador, donde se enfría y vuelve a su estado líquido.
Después, el agua líquida pasa por una pequeña válvula ajustable hacia un evaporador que opera bajo un vacío intenso, de alrededor de seis milibares. A esa presión tan baja, el agua puede evaporarse a tempera…

articles.title: Une photo du visage suffit à cette IA pour repérer les patients atteints de cancer les plus à risque

Une simple photo du visage pourrait-elle aider les médecins à mieux évaluer l'état de santé d'un patient atteint de cancer ? Une étude montre qu'une intelligence artificielle peut identifier dans les traits du visage des signes associés au risque de mortalité, parfois difficiles à apprécier à l'œil nu.
Un visage fatigué, des traits creusés, une apparence plus âgée que l'âge réel… Les médecins savent depuis longtemps que l'apparence physique peut donner des indications sur l'état général d'un patient. Mais une IA pourrait aller plus loin, en quantifiant des signes dont l'importance est difficile à apprécier pour un observateur humain.
C'est ce qu'explorent des chercheurs américains du Mass General Brigham, qui ont développé un système capable d'analyser une photographie du visage pour évaluer le risque de mortalité chez des personnes atteintes de cancer. Leurs résultats ont été publiés le 19 octobre dans The Lancet Digital Health.
Plus de 40 millions de visages pour apprendre à repérer les signes
Baptisée FAHR-Face, cette IA a été entraînée sur plus de 40 millions de photographies issues d'un jeu de données constitué à partir d'images collectées sur Internet. Sa particularité ? Elle a d'abord appris à reconnaître les caractéristiques des visages sans disposer de diagnostics médicaux associés aux photographies. Les chercheurs l'ont ensuite adaptée à deux tâches : estimer "l'âge facial" d'une personne et évaluer le pronostic de patients atteints de cancer.

articles.title: Hackers Hijack Five OVHcloud CLI Releases to Distribute Secret-Stealing Malware
articles.summary:
An attacker used a contributor's GitHub account to replace the download archives on five existing releases of OVHcloud's command-line tool on Monday, October 19. The account had been hijacked, and the new files were a build designed to steal secrets stored on the disk of any machine that runs it, the cloud provider says.
They were live on GitHub for up to 94 minutes, from 12:47 to 14:21 UTC, and reached only people who installed or updated the OVHcloud CLI during that window, via a path that checks for no hash, on macOS, Linux x86_64 or arm64, or Windows x86_64.
OVHcloud deleted the swapped archives and published a clean v0.16.0 that evening as an immutable release, whose files GitHub will not let anyone change. The source code, the release tag, and the company's build pipeline were not touched: the bad build was a plain go build of a later commit, uploaded straight onto releases published between April and September.
Who Was Exposed
On v0.15.0, the attacker replaced six files: the macOS x86_64 and arm64 archives, the Linux x86_64 and arm64 archives, the Windows x86_64 archive, and the checksums.txt file, so the published hashes matched the new binaries. The same six files are now gone from v0.11.0 to v0.14.0 as well. The Linux i386, Windows i386, Windows arm64, and WebAssembly builds were left alone on every release.

Go 1.27.3 and Go 1.26.10, released on October 20, make Go's certificate verifier reject any certificate chain that passes through one of eight intermediate certificate authority keys.
Programs built on the new release will refuse connections to sites and services whose certificates were issued under those keys. The Go team says the keys belong to one certificate authority it has not named, and that it is blocking them because of "specific security concerns around their operation."
It handled the fix on its URGENT track, the one reserved for its most serious issues, and recommends upgrading immediately.
Two days earlier, on October 17, Mozilla added six intermediate certificates issued by eMudhra's emSign Root TLS CA - G3 to OneCRL, the list Firefox uses to block certificates. The Mozilla bug behind those entries is closed to the public, and neither Mozilla nor Go has said what prompted its action. Whether Chrome, Apple, or Microsoft have taken similar action is not established.
Go's change lists only the SHA-256 hashes of the eight keys. A commenter on the Go issue matched all eight to eMudhra intermediates by looking the hashes up in certificate records.
By that matching, six are TLS intermediates issued under the same emSign Root TLS CA - G3 that Mozilla's entries name, and two are code-signing intermediates under emSign Root CS CA - G3:

articles.title: What Security Teams Can Do To Tame Wild Code
articles.summary:
A sales manager builds an AI-assisted workflow to route leads. It connects to customer records, summarizes inbound requests, and posts updates to a shared channel. The workflow saves time, reduces manual work, and soon becomes part of the team’s daily routine. Across the same organization, employees are building useful apps, agents, and automations faster than existing processes can support them.
If you work in security, that success introduces a new set of questions. Whose credentials does the workflow use? Which records can it access? Who can see its output? If it starts exposing information it shouldn’t, can you trace what happened and stop further access?
Wild code takes root when useful builds spread faster than the processes for owning, securing, and maintaining them. It isn’t simply another name for unapproved software. Employees are creating new capabilities, not just adopting existing products. A small experiment can become an operational dependency before security knows it exists.
The risk goes beyond vulnerabilities in generated code. Even code that works as intended can operate with too much access or expose data to the wrong audience:
- Excessive permissions. A workflow needs a small set of records but runs with credentials that can read or modify far more.
- Sensitive data exposure. An employee connects an agent to information it doesn’t need, or makes its output available too broadly. Sensitive information can also end up in model requests or logs.

articles.title: Laver et sécher les serpillières : ce que les robots laveurs font vraiment
articles.summary:
Longtemps cantonnés à l’aspiration des poussières et autres miettes, les aspirateurs robots récents savent aussi laver les sols, retourner seuls à leur station et, pour certains même, gérer une grande partie de leur entretien sans la moindre intervention humaine.
Toutefois, derrière les promesses et des performances toujours plus impressionnantes, tous les robots laveurs ne se valent pas forcément. Voici les critères à examiner avant de choisir son aspirateur robot.
Le robot laveur ne se contente plus de passer un coup de serpillière
Sur le papier, le principe d’un robot laveur reste simple. Il vient aspirer les saletés puis humidifie une ou plusieurs serpillières pour nettoyer le sol. Les générations récentes ont toutefois très largement perfectionné cette seconde étape.
On trouve désormais des systèmes à serpillière fixe, oscillante ou rotative. La première privilégie la simplicité, l’oscillante multiplie les mouvements de frottement tandis que la rotative mise sur une action plus dynamique. Le choix dépend donc aussi du type de salissures rencontrées au quotidien.
Une autre évolution importante concerne la station, qui ne sert plus uniquement à recharger le robot. Sur certains modèles, elle peut remplir le réservoir d’eau propre, récupérer l’eau sale, laver les serpillières et les sécher automatiquement à l’air chaud. Une évolution particulièrement intéressante pour limiter les manipulations entre deux cycles, et optimiser le nettoyage des sols.

Michael Dell doesn't think the memory shortage is anywhere near over. Relief also looks quite far away. New memory fabs take around four years to build, so Dell apparently doesn't expect meaningful new supply until 2029 or 2030.
